review_text:
We have been subscribing for 5+ months so far with the 3-4 year old age range. I have a 2 y/o and 4 y/o and they have loved all of these. Even our friends kids who visit play with the different kits. I'm overall satisfied with the subscription and am going to change it to the 5-7 age range. below are short reviews on each kit we have received.
We got the gears kit and built some of the models. They showed a robot on the bucket however it wasn't in the instruction booklet so we had a blast trying to figure it out as a family. The platforms and gears are sometimes hard to take apart but other then that a good toy, plus it came in a nice hard plastic bucket for storage and additional play.
We received the Automobile Engineer kit and the 4 y/o and his friends love to build the different cars (the book has instructions for at least 4). They either don't want to take it apart or they like to crash it to bits (but that's what boys do). The kit had color coded pieces to indicate different lengths and sizes which is sometimes hard for the kids to differentiate and the instructions aren't written piece by piece. Overall it provides just enough learning with limited adult assistance.
We received the Cod-a-pillar recently and my kids don't play with it. We have limited hard flooring that the kids can play on so it doesn't have room to roam. they both already have remote controlled toys and cars so this is slow and boring waiting for it to turn. Although the most expensive kit so far it's the least enjoyable for our family.
We received the drill and screw peg board thing and it's so much fun for both kids. It comes with interchangeable bits for an electric and hand drill, different color screws and pattern maps. the little one learns dexterity and the use of tools and the older one follows the patterns. They actually play well together on this one and the older one teaches the little one the right pattern. Love this kit! (the drill goes clock wise and counter clock wise to remove screws).
We also received the Math Playbox. It's the most traditional kit since it teaches simple math. the pieces are hard pressed cardboard vice wood (they look like wood on the pic). It requires adult assistance to explain the math principles because it's built like a puzzle and my child just matches the pieces to the holes. It reinforces his numbers and allows him to visualize the math problems. It bores me as an adult but I don't get complaints when I suggest we play with it so I'll take it as a win.

review_text: Love it But One Big Issue. My family has been doing Eat2Explore for over a year now.  We started on Amazon and then switched over to the actual company site.  We have really enjoyed doing it and have liked all of the recipes.  It has been a great experience for our kids.  We love trying all of the new dishes and exploring other cultures through cuisine.  I've paired some of the meals up with our country of study in home school.  We do think it is a bit expensive for what you get.  I noticed a reviewer saying that you get one packet of spices which is not accurate.  You usually get three or four packets (sometimes bottles) of spices, seasonings, sauces, etc.  You also get a small kitchen tool, along with the recipes and shopping lists.  If you sign up through their site, they sometimes offer deals, and we have done the year subscription with a Black Friday discount two years in a row now (currently on our second year).  We have been disappointed this year as we have been receiving duplicate boxes of past meals.  Because of this, we have decided to not do a year subscription next year.  I looked at their site and as of now, they only add 2 new boxes every year.  For the price, we didn't want kits that we have already done.  These kits are in no way a cheap meal (they provide the recipes and harder to find seasonings and you provide pantry staple seasonings and all of the food).  They are for exploring other cultures (and other parts of the U.S. I might add).  We only did it for a few months through Amazon and then a full year and now into our second year, we have already received 3-4 duplicate boxes of past kits.  Each kit has recipes for several meals but we make them all at once and invite other family to join us.  Everyone has loved the meals.  I'm sad to not do it in the future, but there just aren't enough meal kits to sustain keeping the subscription.  Their customer service has been good when we've received broken spice packets, etc.  I recommend this for anyone who wants to make and try new foods.  It's not cheap though, so I would keep that in mind.  Every kit offers vegetarian alternatives with the recipes, which is nice.
product_name: Eat2Explore Subscription Box

Frustrating products for 3-4 year olds - just trying to sell more junk - not curated!. My husband and I both have degrees in the sciences (Chemistry/Computer Science) so I was thrilled to find that Amazon had a Stem Club. But what a disappointment. The first toy that came was a Automobile Engineering kit, with a cute box and a story book. However, the pictures in the story book don't look anything like what you can build and my son was so frustrated (and the story itself was not well written). And while the pieces were bright, the kit was hard to put together, the pictures in the instruction book were hard to follow, the colors didn't match the actual pieces and we all got a bit frustrated with pieces that were the same color but some had odd holes on them and others didn't. For a 3 - 4 year old this was way too hard to navigate, and an older child would find the story line juvenile. The next kit we got had a drill, colored screws and a white tray with holes on it. This was somewhat better, as pattern cards were included. Unfortunately, wasn't very interesting. The third kit was a cheaply executed maze game that you put together.

This club doesn't seem to be actually curated. I think it is more likely Amazon getting a premium from some lesser known "toy" vendors to include their products. Very disappointed, canceled after third box.

I have a wide, Mexican face and I'm fine with them. Like most sheet masks, I do sometimes cut extra slits around the eye holes so they lay flatter against my face instead of being stretched across.

My 3rd envelop should be arriving soon and I don't see myself unsubscribing any time soon.

review_text:
Great Package of High Quality Tea Leaves with Reusable Tea Bags. I loved this, and they had the perfect first package sampler with Lady Grey, Formosa Oolong, Gen Mai Cha, and Blood Orange tisane.

Although I am an admirer of many teas, I am usually no longer a devotee of Earl Grey/Lady Grey blends. Years ago, I was a huge fan of Earl Grey, but over the years and after taste-testing some truly terrible bergamot-infused teas calling themselves "_____ Grey," I have found that I am no longer as excited about Earl Grey or Lady Grey teas. However, the Lady Grey was charming in this case, with a much more subtle bergamot and lavender that was not overly floral to create a very nice, smooth mouthfeel and flavor.

My favorite from this first box is the Formosa Oolong which I found to be very smooth, with the perfect amount of astringency to make a smooth overall Oolong with a slight muscatel crispness on the back of the tongue. Not my favorite in the world, but certainly an excellent Oolong.

The Gen Mai Cha was very nice, earthy, and warm with that traditional smoked popcorn-type flavor unique to that blend. And the Blood Orange tisane was a nice rounding-out of the four selections with a traditional hibiscus-based fruit tisane with a lovely blood orange flavor.

The only thing I would suggest for the company to improve is to consider that people who are not wholly new to tea are ordering this. Reading the backs of some of the packages felt like they were leaving out more important information such as altitude, estate, or specific tasting notes in favor of information that felt almost patronizing.

I appreciated the disposable tea bags, as I usually purchase those from OzarkMoons.net to brew my looseleaf teas. I'm sure other customers who do not have a lot of tea equipment will appreciate them as well.

Overall, I thought this was a lovely package, and I will be continuing my subscription for this tea sampler! Thank you!
product_name: Simple Loose Leaf Tea Subscription Box

review_text:
Quality over quantity. I would really emphasize that this packages provides delicious high quality teas, but not necessarily a large quantity. Personally, I think the variety plus the quality is worth the price. In the box I received four different teas (all quite delicious and flavorful) and the tea in each packet will provide three first seeps. So, if you seep your tea only once, you will get about twelve cups. But, all the teas I received were good enough to seep at least one more time. So, i got about 24 cups of tea out of the packets received. If you only seep your tea once, you may not feel like you are getting your money's worth and you won't get the full value out of the tea.
Also, to get the good flavor, you will need to follow the instructions and not over seep or use too hot of water. I found that when I set the timer and paid attention to the instructions, the tea was really good. One cup I let it seep too long and it killed the flavor.
I have only received one box so far and it had an Assam tea, floral tea, spicy tea, and chocolate tea. They covered four different flavors, which was a nice variety. My favorite was the Black Tea Melted Chocolate. I also really enjoyed the Organic Assama-zing tea. The Blackened Heart had nice hints of rose, it was very smooth, goes bitter if seeped too long. Mexican Hot chocolate is okay, but very strong. I am ending up with extra cups because I'm using a smaller amount of tea per cup. Also, I'm having to experiment with adding extra sugar or cream to really enjoy it.

Excellent Toys for Learning STEM Concepts. I was worried about the quality of the toys that my kids would receive when I signed up for STEM club based on some of the reviews, but after two months I have been surprised with activities. Engineering is more than following instructions on a sheet of paper, it is about taking concepts and applying them in new ways to build something new. The toys I have received so far for my girls are the type of toys that are fun for them to play with, but also provides that "spark" that will help them to think of intuitive new ways to build things. review_text:

I'm not completely satisfied. Product for most recent delivery is much better than last one. Last one wasn't much different than item that was sent prior, in my opinion. Purpose of STEM Education is to explore various concepts and engage audience. Repeating concepts may be good for someone who's going to be quizzed/tested. But considering this if for kids. I was somewhat annoyed that concepts were repeated and there wasn't anything new. It just went from "magic" to "kitchen". However, last kit is much more improved, as I stated earlier. It's a mechanics kit (levers, linkages, and structures). This is what I expect. Diversity in STEM concepts and material.

Product so far, is nice overall. All items needed are in place. Very few items to do the interactive activity need to be replenished if I do this project with my kids. The items that would need to be replenished can easily be found in local grocery stores and really cheap. review_text:
8-13 is bad. Others great.. I have had a great experience in the quality of the lower age toys; however, this first month adding 8-13 is extremely disappointing. This "mechanics" set is filled with quizzes and lessons but none of the projects are actually mechanically sound. Beyond that, every project we have tried has had a minimum of 3 errors in the diagram to the point where the instructions actually contradict themselves.

Finally, (and this was the last straw for me) the "catapult" used as an example of a lever was supposed to be used by flipping it with a finger. Catapults use tension (and levers) but even though it would have been idiotically simple to add a rubber band, these "STEM experts" were apparently happier to ignore the concept of tension and just flick the toy across the room. And let's be real: a catapult is a poor example in the first place considering a trebuchet far better illustrates the concept.

Obviously this toy is meant to capitalize on parents who like the idea of STEM toys but have no actual experience in the field of physics or engineering while filling your child's head with incomplete theories and bad science.

Ugh.

But the 3-8 is great :) we'll be keeping those two.

review_text: The Best Science Subscription I've Had. I am a home school science teacher with a MS degree in Chemistry.  I LOVE science and have subscribed to a couple other science programs, such as Spangler Science and Magic School Bus.  I was curious as to what Amazon might include in the STEM subscription, so I took my chances.  Well, this is by far the BEST subscription I've ever had!  The other subscriptions got old after a year, and my kids rarely were interested in the boxes we received; I always cancelled the subscription after a year.  With the Amazon STEM program, we receive really interesting, fun, inspiring kits and toys, many way more valuable than the monthly subscription price!  I am enjoying this subscription so much that I have no intention of stopping it.  I have received items such as a wind generator kit (not one of those tiny ones, but a HUGE one that stands a few feet tall!), physics kits, construction kits, Smart Circuits, a National Geographic Fossil kit, a large dinosaur model kit, and several other really cool things. I'm like a kid at Christmas every month!  I have not received any kits that involve wet chemistry or biology, but many have involved experiments in the physical sciences. If you love all kinds of science and have students or children with whom you are willing to share your "toys" and love of science, this subscription is the one you've been looking for!

review_text:
Fantastic Concept and I Love it!! (Updated 4/29/22). One of the FAQ's state,
How will I know what album I'll be receiving? "After you subscribe, visit the Returns & Orders page to see which album you'll receive this month. If you aren't interested in the album on its way, go to the Manage Your Subscriptions page and click 'skip this box' to skip the month's album".

With the first two albums I received, my first notification was when the Amazon truck dropped them off at my house. With my third album, my first notification was via an email when Amazon thanked me for my recent order. I logged in to see what I ordered, since I didn't remember ordering anything.

All three of the albums I received are albums I would never purchase,
1. The Clash - London Calling, not something I would enjoy and I returned it.
2. Van Valen - Van Halen, which was actually pretty good and I remember purchasing it went it was released. I may end up keeping this album.
3. Rolling Stones - Exile On Main Street, which is rated #1 or #2 most popular album of the Rolling Stones, depending on which website you use. Not a big fan of this album and I will be returning it.

I would much rather had received the Rolling Stones, Sticky Fingers, album versus Exile on Main Street, since I would listen to it repeatedly and never returned it.

Wild Horses, Brown Sugar, Can't You Hear Me Knocking are some of my favorite songs of all time. I can listen to these songs over and over.

Do not get me wrong, the three albums I received are outstanding albums of the 70's and 80's, but they are not the type of music I enjoy. I would play them once and never play them again, so I will return them.

As I said, the concept is an outstanding and a fantastic idea, especially, since was I was lead to believe I would be receiving albums by the following artists, according to the Amazon web page, https://www.amazon.com/Vinyl-Month-Club-Golden-Subscription.
1. Mile Davis - I already have most of Miles Davis albums.
2. Led Zeppelin - I love Led Zeppelin
3. Fleetwood Mac - I love the early Fleetwood Mac
4. Aretha Franklin - Songs I grew up listening to and I already have most of her albums.
5. Pink Floyd - The Dark Side of the Moon, Meddle, Animals, Wish You Were Here, The Wall, all fantastic albums !!

I read where some people received Pink Floyd albums, The Dark Side of the Moon or The Wall. I would really enjoy receiving them versus what I already received.

Update - I received The Wall, in March, and I already have The Dark Side of the Moon on a SACD, plus the Immersion Box Set. Every time I play the "multi channel" SACD version of The Dark Side of the Moon, it sounds like Pink Floyd is playing my living room. Each instrument is playing on a separate speaker. Lower the lights, turn up the volume, close your eyes, and enjoy the music!!

I am a big music lover, so the Vinyl of the Month Club is a perfect fit for me. Iron out the kinks and it will be a big success .

1. Purchase some of the toys to determine which TYPES of toys the kids like.
2. Is AGE LEVEL indicated appropriate for YOUR child.
3.Do you want to provide SUPERVISION, be INVOLVED w/your child to the degree needed.
4. Do you want the same type product monthly or change.
5. Is price a better value this way or if purchased as child is ready or if child EARNS it as in when ready for next stage.
These are my recommendations for how to view the reviews of those who HAVE purchased the STEM program. When/if I DO sign any of my Gkids up for it, I'll evaluate it in detail. I hope this won't be rejected because I haven't purchased the program. Knowing HOW to make the decision based on the reviews of others is important. I make this statement as a physician who had spent MANY YEARS reading copious medical journals deciding how patients will best benefit from products w/o being influenced by the hype of advertising but on the basis of what is best for the INDIVIDUAL patient sitting in front of me. review_text:
I am NOT exaggerating when I say this is some of the best tea I've ever had. I love tea. One might say I have an obsession. I have about 47 million tea bags stashed around my house. (is THAT an exaggeration? The world may never know...)
Anyway the shipping on this box was FAST - even to Guam! Usually boxes from Amazon arrive via a singular man in a rowboat, 8 weeks after ordering. This box came less than a week later though so they must have flagged down an airplane. And the TEA! oh man. I got the following flavors, and loved all of them:
1) Blood Orange Herbal - a rooibos base with delicious notes of orange and vanilla. Truly a flavor explosion as promised. So delightful and amazing for fall!
2) Genmaicha Green Tea - how delighted I was to find itty bitty pieces of popcorn in my loose tea along with toasted hulled rice kernals! Sounds weird, tastes AMAZING. a nice earthy toasty flavor.
3) Blue Lady Grey - Earl Grey is my favorite type of tea, but this may have changed my mind. It has added lavender and is perfect for a pick me up that is also calming. Which I need in my desk job.
4) Qi Lan Oolong - I literally took one sip of this and audibly exclaimed OH MY GOD THIS IS AMAZING. I wish I could describe it to you here, but there just aren't words. i'll try. It's like angels kissed some oolong tea leaves and then blessed them with kittens and flowers. Seriously. It's earthy but floral, soothing and DELISH.

I highly, highly recommend this box of tea. It's cheap and the tea quality is so good, I don't even know how they're making a profit. Perhaps they aren't. Perhaps they're just doing the greatest act of service the world has ever known.

review_text:
Interesting Idea But Odd Implementation - Not The Best Value for Me. Overall, the box was decent but not exceed my expectations. I like the idea that if you see a box on their website that you like, you can go ahead and get it at a great discount compared to full retail price for the items when purchased individually. I see no advantage to buying this on Amazon rather than the GQ site. It might be easier to cancel through Amazon? If I had purchased through GQ site directly, I would actually have received a free bonus item, a pair of socks.

I ordered a box in May 2019 which was delivered on June 1. I expected that the first box delivered would be the summer edition that had not yet been released. I was a bit disappointed when the box arrived with with the spring items that had already been revealed on GQ site, Instagram, and other subscription blogs. This completely eliminated the surprise factor of the subscription box for new items. My initial reaction was negative since I had already seen the items inside online! If I had known that this box would be the spring box, I would not have purchased it. If you like the items pictured on the GQ site, go ahead and order! If not, hold off for the next quarter.

Part of what lead to my expectation that I would receive the summer box was that it wasn't going to be delivered immediately like normal prime items. Seeing the expected delivery of June made it seem like these would be summer items. It appears that these ship out in batches each month with the same boxes for a three month window.

Specific to the Spring box (MSA blog valued this box at ~$177):

I liked getting to try new toiletry items such as shaving cream and moisturizer, however I felt that this box was too focused on this type of item. The website and product description (estimated box value) made it seem like the box would include full size items. However, the box shipped with mostly trial size items - the bar of soap was full size. Great if you are interested in trying new toiletries but don't expect full size packages.

I have used the mophie battery pack a few times. Always nice to have another spare charger. I would not have specifically purchased this brand or paid full price for it.

The Hims gummy bear supplement was an interesting idea - However this had a significant amount of sugar and was basically gummy bears + emergen-C/Airborne. I expected that this would be a gummy vitamin. I opened the bottle and these smelled awful - I gave these away at work.

The bluetooth speaker was not what I expected. The color in all the GQ website images was black, however the one I received was blue. Additionally, the blue color did not match the color on the packaging and was very shiny which made it look cheap. I already have a bluetooth speaker. I didn't need an additional one so I gave this away as well.

review_text:

I wish there were options for the tampons that come in the box. For example, I need mostly light tampons, some regulars, and a few supers, as well as some overnight pads (it is a really bad idea to sleep with a tampon in). This box came with only regular tampons. The other items that came were a handful of liners, scented feminine wipes, one pain killer (acetaminophen), a serum face mask, an eye mask, 4 bags of raspberry leaf tea, 2 Ferrero Rochers, and a wafer chocolate called a "knopper".

Over all, it's a well curated box, but it doesn't replace me having to go to the store to get tampons and pads. There are also things that I would never use, such as the scented feminine wipes (a bad idea for any person with a vagina), tea in a tea bag, and the pain killer that could interfere with my medications. Some people may be able to use this box, but I think it is not for me. I would rather make my own kit that has things I will actually use.

review_text:

So, overall, worth about $118, which is just a handful of dollars more than I payed for it.

They could have at least had a camping hammock, or a tactical backpack. The fact that this box is themed around tactical gear, but I got a pick-nick kit instead, was really disappointing. I was expecting survival gear, not lounging gear.

It had a few regular pads and tampons (not enough for a full period, but enough to get by until you can get to the store), a couple of overnight pads and super tampons, a handful of pantyliners, a couple of patches for period cramps, and wipes for bloodstains (love those). The next box had different cramp patches and no bloodstain wipes. Instead, there were snacks in this box (banana chips, granola bites, and chocolate)
Overall, I like the other various items I got in the box, especially the CBD massage oil that was in every box (It's amazing!). It seems like everything together is worth about $45 to $55, so it's not getting a deal, and is actually rather pricey considering I got the pampered ($80).

On one hand, it is a really useful bag, on the other hand, if I was to keep this subscription box for a year, I would have 12 bags. I have uses for all three I have gotten, but I'm going to run out of uses eventually. It would be helpful if the bags were different in every box. The bags being the same makes it hard to tell them apart and harder to find things.

I liked getting a few of these boxes, but I just can't justify keeping this subscription. If there were enough products for a full period, a comprehensive period emergency kit, a different bag every month, and the extra items in every box, I could see keeping it. As is, it just isn't worth it every month. That said, it is a nice treat once in a while.

review_text:
Some folks are missing the point. The way I see this box is that it’s for curated things that I wouldn’t usually buy. For example, in the Spring box, I received a Reily throw that is sold for $70-80 on the seller website. It’s very high quality and felt great and immediately became my favorite throw - and I wouldn’t normally pay that much for a blanket! The other items in the box were nice to have. As for the Summer box, the sunglasses are very high quality and they’re sold for $115 on the brand website. I haven’t heard about that brand before but was really impressed by the quality and looked up their other models. The same box contained a $60 retinol eye cream, and I normally wouldn’t pay that much for an eye cream! So it’s a good chance to try to see if it’s worth it. The waterproof packs are very useful to keep credit card, ID, and cash when, for example, going to the beach and I don’t want to carry my wallet.

Opinions are divided on the usefulness of the items and I totally agree, and didn’t expect, that not everything in the box is useful or needed at all! But if the goal is to receive items that I would usually buy on my own, then I wouldn’t subscribe and just go buy what I need!

review_text: It was worth trying.. I subscribed because of the Amazon deal where my first box would only cost $3. I was pleasantly surprised by the sturdy packaging and amount of tea I received. Since I already have strainers for brewing loose leaf tea, I have not tried the bags which came in the box. As for the teas, I received Blood Orange Herbal, Blue Lady Grey, QiLan Oolong, and Genmaicha. I really enjoyed the herbal tea (rooibos, orange peel, hibiscus, rosehips, apple pieces, safflowers, rose petals, and orange/vanilla/lemon flavor) and would buy it again on its own. The black tea (whole leaf black tea, blue mellow blossoms, lavender flowers, and bergamot flavor) was pretty good, although I already have other Earl and Lady Grey teas that I enjoy. I found the oolong to be okay and drinkable, but will probably pass it on to a friend. The Genmaicha (bancha green tea, popped corn and toasted hulled rice kernels) was horrible on all counts. Upon opening it smelled odd as though something was old or rancid, but I decided to give it a go anyway.  After forcing three sips I had to pour it out. I don't know if I got a bad bag or I just don't have a taste for that blend, but I'm throwing the rest of the bag in the trash. While I enjoyed this box experience (for the most part), I'll be cancelling my subscription since it's a better deal for me to buy tea that I can see, smell and ideally sample first.

* Chicken treats.
* A little bunny thing with 2 puffballs.

1. review_text:
One of the best beauty sub boxes out there!. Pictured above is my first box, sometime last year when it was only $15. Price is now $23, with free shipping still. I’ve loved everything they’ve sent so far, including amazing brands like Sunday Riley, Akar, AHC, and many more that I never would have splurged on or known about otherwise. Before Allure, my skincare routine was practically nonexistent, and quite frankly boring. Using the same drugstore face wash, makeup, moisturizer, and beauty products wasn’t exactly exciting. Now my skincare routine is SO much better, and I definitely look forward to using fun, new items every month. So far, I’ve gotten face wash (including an AMAZING face bar by Erno Laslo, sp?) moisturizer, oils, pimple patches, nail appliqués, face masks, eye masks, hair cream, hair protective spray, highlighter, eyeshadow, eyeliner, mascara,, sunscreen, lipstick, toner, and just... so many things. They NEVER send you the same product twice, and I absolutely love the full size products and small size products are perfect for traveling. I love that you can preview the next month’s box and skip if you don’t think you’ll like it too. I check the value on every product, and there’s been MANY times where one product alone is worth well over the cost of the box.

New member gift when signing up, and a huge box if you sign up for a year at a time. Great Facebook community (Allure Beauty Box subscribers) where members discuss items in their box and sell or swap their stashes. Every box comes with a booklet that gives hints and tips on how to use the products, as well as coupon codes if you wish to purchase more.

I’ve since subscribed to BoxyCharm as well, and they’re both a great value for the money. BoxyCharm is more tailored to your quiz results, while Allure is pretty much one size fits all, with slight variations, like brown or black eyeliner for instance. Both send notifications upon shipment, and I’ve never had anything arrive broken or unable to use.

Overall, great box! Really happy I went with it!

I have very mixed feelings about this whole subscription:
Pros: the colors of product/kitchen tool is vibrant and bright. Everything my daughter has received so far has been good quality and I've actually used hers instead.

The products ARE quality, like I mentioned above, I even enjoy using them at times. BUT the choice of tools AND the recipes are way out there for the most part and NOT something beginner little chefs would even WANT to eat, let alone spending their time learning to try to make.
Which brings my next con...I've noticed the grocery product list get pretty pricey and are not always sold in every day grocery stores or in smaller quantities. Instead, you end up either going from store to store, buying it on Amazon/somewhere online and wait days for arrival, or your young chef gives up and the recipe is never made, which brings you back to comments about price and kids really wanting to learn to cook.
I gave this a try for a solid year before canceling. What was even more sad is my now 14 yr old loved getting a fun surprise each month but didn't bat an eye, yell/fight about deciding to cancel etc, instead was actually happy about it bc she said she felt guilty about receiving something she never used. I could have purchased her ... anything else with the money wasted on this subscription. Heck, I could have and should have (maybe I still will) actual cooking lessons from one of the local grocers. review_text:
This "Service" is a Ripoff and Customer Service is a Joke!. I subscribed to Pusheen Box back in Summer of 2020 because I wanted something to cheer us up while we were all stuck in our homes and unable to go or do anything due to my husband's job. The first box (Summer), was fine, but it had some issues in shipping making its way to us. That's fine, most of the items in the box were cute and seemed to be mostly well made.

Both Fall and Winter boxes (2020) had shipping issues and it took over two weeks to get to us, despite being shipped FedEx. Items in the box were mixed; the clothing items were of quality, but almost everything else in the boxes outside of the figurines was dollar store or knock-off quality that you'd see for sale in a a dollar store or from a "third-party" vendor from China here on Amazon. Numerous people complained that their electronic lantern in the fall box was broken and didn't work... Pusheen Box did not offer refunds to anyone... and instead told them to go find EXTREMELY specific battery brands to use in the lantern (which didn't fix the problem). The Winter Box had dollar store salt and pepper shakers and "wine" glasses. The glasses I received were imperfect and had bubbles trapped in the glass. The decals were placed over glasses with nub defects (small bits of glass sticking out of an otherwise smooth surface). No refunds or replacements were offered to anyone with these issues or if they were, people never GOT the replacements they were promised.

Fast forward to Spring 2021. The box was charged to my account on March 17. The box's release was delayed with NO REASON given by the company.. so it didn't even "ship" until April 28th. I didn't get any tracking information until May 4th... and it's been stuck in limbo with no updates and several "delivery" dates that have been passed on.

Add to that that you can't get a hold of ANYONE at their customer support. You send an email into the void and you MIGHT get a response 5 days later that is cursory and mostly doesn't answer your complaints or questions. It's May 19th now... and I still have no Spring Box, STILL have not heard back from customer service despite THREE SEPARATE tickets being launched. I have only received ONE response about tracking not updating.. and that was on May 14th. NOTHING since then, my package is still lost... and you can't even call up FedEx to look into it because Culture Fly (the company that runs these boxes) has a "sticky" on all the boxes, stating that the receiver (me) has to contact them (the sender) to launch an investigation... but how am I supposed to that when you NEVER REPLY TO YOUR EMAILS?!?!

So subpar service, SLOW delivery times, lost packages and declining quality of items in just 9 months... I do NOT recommend anyone purchase a sub from this company. Do yourself a favor and look up other reviews about this company on other review aggregate sites. It's not pretty. I wish I had.

review_text:
I cannot stress this enough. I bought a single one time box on amazon at Christmas for the fuzzbucket. I was honestly far more impressed than I thought I would be. I then started a subscription with Barkbox directly.
The customer service this company has cannot be surpassed. Seriously. I have a 90 monster who is “dainty” when it comes to his toys. He wants the little boy toys and the big boy treats. He believes that toys that are made for his size are far too big for his delicate little mouth, so he wants the tinier toys. But don’t you dare skimp on his treat size, he’s not that dainty! Dogs are weird.
Anyway, they helped to customize his boxes so they come to his liking. The toys are very well made and quite clever honestly. He gets the normal ones, so I cannot attest to the durability of the super chewer box. And let’s face it, if your dog wants the stuffing, the squeaker, or the crinkle out; the stuffing, squeaker, and crinkle ARE coming out.
The dog loves his bark boxes. I know the day they get delivered, when I come through the back door after work the dog will frantically herd me to the front door to get the mail. Once I get the box in, the dog noses at it until I get it open, while the cat lies in wait behind the sofa to pounce out and claim the box the moment it empties.
The thought and work they put into designing these themes is amazing. It’s not just a couple of themed toys and treats, they’ve also got cleverly designed box liners (last month was gym themed, the liner had an elaborate and cute step by step exercise sheet for your dog to do) and a little booklet for the humans to be amused by (last months shaped like a vcr tape box with a dog dressed like Richard Simmons and a tape shaped insert that slid out). On the inside of every box there is also an amusing little cartoon dog saying something punny. He’s kind of hidden, it took a few months before I saw him.
Honestly, for the price, you will get good quality toys, a couple of bags of treats, and a chew that your dog will love. If your dog doesn’t love something, they will replace it. If your dog immediately destroys a toy, they will replace it with a more durable one.
If your unsure about the quality of the toys or treats, you can order an individual one from their website. The same goes for the treats.
I honestly spend a lot less on my dog since I’ve started this subscription. I’d go to Petco every month for his treats and come out with a bagful of cheap crappy toys and about $100 lighter. Now he gets a few long lasting durable toys he loves and some treats to boot and I don’t have to go to petco!

The "College" themed box included a bag of treats, a catnip "textbook" toy, a kicker stick that looks like a brick library building, two hard bouncy "atom" balls, and a pom-pom ended toy that has a bungee cord so if the cat pulls hard enough at the pom-pom treats you've loaded inside will drop. The last had a velcro loop on top so you could hang it, and it says it's adjustable as to how hard they have to pull if your cats dig it.
For my cats, the catnip book has been a hit, the building toy was meh, the atom balls are amusing but they're hard rubber so they won't pick them up and we'll see if they play soccer with them. The pom-pom toy was amusing as a dancer toy, but they haven't pulled hard enough to release treats from it yet. It's a short tube with a short line to the pom-pom so it's not a great dancer toy. Only one of my cats will eat the treats.
That's 2.5 - 3 out of 5 successes for my house. There's no customization, so I figured it wouldn't be all wins, and there was a variety of types of toy which is great. However, according to their math on the insert, the value of the items adds up to $25. If the subscriber price for the box is $20 and not everything tickles your fancy, you might as well just go to PetCo. Having a curated theme and a box that is a nice nap spot doesn't feel like it adds a whole lot of value.

Gourmet Cookies & Organic Coffee Oh my!. In my never ending search for more and more, and more organic coffee I stumbled into this subscription box. I've tried other subscription coffees on Amazon, those that will not be named here, but they did not offer organic coffee. With one service you may get organic coffee from time to time and with the other service there was just no option.
The idea of getting 2 cookies paired with a great roast of organic coffee seems like a perfect combo with the only negative thing being that it leaves me wanting more and more, and more...
The cookies are always bakery fresh and individually sealed. They are a decent size and always taste amazing. Every cookie that I have had to date from this service is always fresh, delicious, and leaves me wanting more.
The coffee is where it's at and was my main focus. While I do not like any flavored coffee, I always love trying different roasts of coffee from different places. It amazes me how coffee can taste so different even though from the outside it's "just coffee". It's fun getting a box with bright green shredded paper for packaging every month filled with 2 small packages, which is now 1 bigger package of coffee and 2 cookies.
The coffee comes freshly ground and sealed in the multi-layer pouch. I don't notice any valves on these pouches to release the gas that ground coffee can emit, but given that it is so freshly ground and you will probably drink it up fast I guess this isn't a big deal. I believe the coffee would last a year as they do seem to be vacuum sealed with no room for anything to get in there or out until you break open the seal and inhale the fragrant & freshly roasted coffee. I don't think there is any better smell than ground coffee. Maybe fresh baked cookies? No, on second thought, coffee smells better and is so much better for you, usually (depending on how you enjoy your coffee).

review_text: Not Appropriate For Age Group Specified.. I was looking for a monthly book subscription for my granddaughter. I have to side with the people who said the books were not well-chosen for the specified audience. I picked 0-12 months. One book was a board book and it was about the nose. It was cute. The other two were not for a 6-month old. One was a "First Reader" with small peel off stickers to place in the book. The other was nursery rhymes, but more of the Grimm's variety. No rhyme, no meter, and one was about pulling off a guys legs. Definitely not age appropriate. I ended up just buying a bunch of books from Amazon with 10,000+ reviews, 4.8+ stars, and rated by customers on age group appropriateness. I ended up with a great list of well-known and loved books. Now I'll just send her some each month. It took a little longer and some research, but in the end I think it will be well worth it. Reading is too important to start them out with "just whatever". I want all the book spines to be worn and cracked and the pages falling out from how often it was read. Not used under a short leg on a bedside table to keep it from wobbling. :)

review_text:
Deceptive and Horrid Customer Experience. I've probably tried about 4-5 boxes from GQ over the past 3 years. Here's what I learned: often you're receive the same free samples they hand out in a mall, except now you're paying for them. Once in a while, you'll get a full size product, and rarely it'll be something you'll enjoy.

The other items that you'd expect in the box are actually index cards with coupon codes where you're supposed to redeem them for "free" items. Well, let me explain what in reality happens: half the sizes/colors aren't available when you go to redeem your coupon, and often, these aren't items that the retailer normally sells -- they're thinner, cheaper, less desirable versions specially made for GQ. You want to redeem your free shirt in Large, and prefer blue? Too bad: you'll get size small in white.

Another deception: last quarter they gave a code for a "free pair of Bombas sock". Guess what? The socks are free, but Bombas bangs you for $5 to ship them, so that's in addition to the $50 you wasted on the GQ Box.

And here's also where the wheels fall off: they regularly forget to pack items in the box. You can call them and they'll try to help, but sometimes they have nothing left.

My last box also provided my a coupon code for a free pair of underwear, but they provided a broken link to redeem them. I called and the rep couldn't help so now I'm waiting for a manager to resolve. It's a Mickey Mouse operation from top to bottom.

I love the concept, but the execution is just piss poor. Save your money.
product_name: GQ Box

review_text: Wanted to love this.... First off, I want to say that this program could be an amazing, old school record club with a few improvements. Right now though, it's not quite right. Last month I was excited to receive an updated copy of Pink Floyd's "Darkside of the Moon", noting it on my orders page prior to shipping. A few days later Amazon cancelled the shipment due to a carrier issue and rather than reship it or send something new, they refunded the monthly fee. That's fine, but it's a record club so just send a new one or something different rather than cancelling out the entire month's shipment. This month my next album showed up on my order screen, CCR's Greatest Hits which isn't an album I currently have, so I was happy to get it. I clicked on the album link to see what songs were included and noticed that the album's current selling price through Amazon is actually less than the monthly club price which is problematic. As this is a club format, getting whatever album Amazon chooses is part of fun and excitement, however paying more than what I would if I'd just picked the album and ordered myself, not so much. I've cancelled the club for now, but will rejoin if Amazon figures out how to work through some of the challenges this program currently has.

review_text: Cute as a gift, but not great quality tea. On one of the text inserts that came with the box, they said that they aren't actually a tea company, they are a gift company. And that is exactly right. It's a cute gift, nicely packaged, but the tea is very subpar. We drink a lot of tea and my husband recently gave up caffeine, so I got him this box to sample lots of herbal teas to see what he might like. I think there are suposed to be 5 tsp per tea for 20 cups of tea total, but they are consistently underfilled (4 tsp per bag) and when brewed, they are consistently really weak teas. Usually loose leaf tea is nicer than bagged tea with full leaves and fresh ingredients. However, the teas are more like the bottom of the barrel and more dust than leaves. We have a micromesh strainer for rooibos so that you don't end up drinking the "splinters", but this tea is so dusty and tiny that it escaped the cotton bag and metal filters. It really should be reserved for low quality bags. Normally brewing rooibos, it gets nice and dark in 3-5 minutes rich with flavor, but this never gets really dark and tastes so watered down even when brewed exactly like similar teas from other companies. We had this subscription for 4 months now and while it's cute and the tea flavors sound good with a good variety, they are all just so WEAK compared to very similar flavors and types of teas from other companies. Even the hibiscus tea didn't get dark red or have flavor. It just makes me think that the tea is really old and broken down, or whatever leftovers there were that couldn't be sold to higher quality companies. I wanted to love this box, but am just disapointed. They say you should have 20 cups of tea with 1 tsp each. We have a 1 tsp tea scoop from vhadam (a really good quality tea company that also has an amazon subscription) and the bags are consistenyly only filled with 4 tsp. With how weak it is, you really have to use double that and you can't really rebrew since it's so weak already, so ou really only get 2-4 cups per type of tea (8-16 total instead of 20).

VALUE!!!. My usual medium is oil paint so I was a bit skeptical.

I needn’t have been. This kit is BRILLIANT! Not only does it provide art lessons I will take into my oil paintings, it’s beginner friendly enough that my 16 year old (who has never even shown any interest in art at ALL) is excited to try it. The paints are brilliantly colored, and I LOVE that part of this is (perhaps unintentionally) teaching color theory to beginners. My first kit has 2 BEAUTIFUL, vibrant, colorful projects, and it teaches how to mix the base colors-red blue yellow- and black and white to create every color needed in the pieces.

Everything needed to complete the projects was included. Canvases. Brushes. Paints. Someone who has NEVER painted but has seen or been inspired by Bob Ross could pick this kit up and knock out a beautiful piece of art on their first try.

I’m very VERY impressed with this kit for the price. Very worth it. I will be maintaining my subscription for the foreseeable future!!!

review_text:
Three boxes in, and things aren't looking too good.. The Deadpool Box was fairly uninspiring. The Pop! was great, but the rest, not so much.

I loved the Venom box. Great pose for Venom, nice shirt, neat pint-size, decal. Your mileage may vary, but it was a step up, I thought.

The First Ten Years box? This one makes me wonder if Funko is even involved in curating the items. Funko boxes used to look like boxes for fans, by fans. But this latest looks like it was planned by someone with little investment in the community.

For starters, how about that centerpiece? Iron Man vs. Whiplash. If you like Iron Man 2, great. None of the Marvel films have been absolute stinkers, not even Dark World. But Iron Man 2 isn't at the top of people's lists. And, perhaps more to the point, it is not worth commemorating in a celebration of Marvel Studios first ten years. Why not surprise and delight customers and do a Movie Moments diorama with Thor coming down on Cap's shield? Or if that already exists, surely there's something else out there. Even an exclusive Thanos Pop! marking some significant moment from Infinity War would have been a more fitting thing.

As for the rest of the items, I don't think Pint-Size are bad, or even the Pez, but the characters are not immediately recognizable in gold, and I had to look at the back of the package (with characters in color) to recognize Thor. And between the Pez and one of the Pint-Size, you've got two items from Ragnarok!

No Cap, no Guardians, and a lot of wasted space for Whiplash. People will always disagree about the class of item included, but the themes should always make sense. And for a box advertised as a celebration of the first ten years of Marvel Studios, this is an utter failure.

review_text:
Best subscription out there!. We just hit one year of our subscription and plan to keep it going for quite a while! We started it when our son was 7.5 years old (the 8-13 year old STEM club). These are the items we have received so far:
Smartivity Mechanical Xylofun Music Machine
Constructechs Educational Engineering DIY Remote Control 2 in 1 Space Racer
Thames & Kosmos Optical Science
SmartLab Toys Ultimate Secret Formula Lab
Thames & Kosmos Wind Power 2.0
OWI Kingii Dragon Robot Science Kit
Thames & Kosmos Physics Workshop
National Geographic Mega Fossil Mine
SmartLab Toys Smart Circuits Games & Gadgets Electronics Lab
Engino Discovering Stem: Levers, Linkages & Structures Building Kit

There have also been two months with ThinkFun games (Gravity Maze and Laser Maze). We absolutely love ThinkFun games in our home, and have many of them, so we cancelled the orders before they shipped since we already had those two particular ones.

The variety of items has been incredible. The prices can't be beat! I check out each item we get on Amazon and the cheapest one has been $25, all the way up to $40+, for the subscription fee of only $20. The quality of items has been wonderful as well. The Engino set was such a huge hit that my son requested more for birthday and Christmas. He plays with the Engino sets more than Legos now! I think he is up to 5 of the sets, and they all work together.

You CAN see what is coming before it ships. The items are ordered on the same day each month. If you check your order page you can see what is going to be coming and cancel it if you want before it ships. It is a very small time window, but it is very possible if you choose. The value and quality we receive far outweighs any perceived inconvenience for checking the order page once a month.

I have recommended the Amazon STEM Club to many people as I feel it's one of the best subscription services of any kind based on the value and quality. We have not had experience with the younger subscriptions, but I can vouch for the 8-13 year old one. I definitely think that age range is appropriate. Our 7.5 year old was able to do most of the first several sets that came, but he has needed parental assistance for a good number of them. We've just turned it into a fun weekly activity - "Maker Monday". We make some tea together and have fun with the sets. These aren't "once-and-done" type sets. There is a lot of longevity in most of them, different builds, different experiments, etc. It's been a great experience to share together. :)

To be fair- about half of the kits were ok, but rarely in the same month for my two kids. I had to skip months to stock up on the acceptable kits so that one of my kids was not left out due to an effectively unusable STEM kit. With the disappointing kits and the stream of returns I had to manage, it was a monthly hassle I started to really dread.

review_text:
Low quality tea. Not impressed at all.. When my first box came in, I immediately brewed all four teas, with each one yielding approximately 8 cups.

The teas included were an Oolong, a lavender Earl Gray, a Green Tea with rice in it, and an orange herbal Rooibos tea.

The Earl Gray was very mild and not bad. It doesn't even rank in the top ten Earl Grays that I have had, though. It's probably the best of the four teas that came in the box.

The Oolong Tea was pretty strong, musky, and smelled terrible. I turned it into iced tea to control some of the pungent aroma. When chilled, it's not bad as a sipping tea, but I certainly wouldn't want to try it again.

The Green Tea was pretty unremarkable. It was filled with grains of rice, which didn't add much of anything to the brew. I added some lemon and honey to make it more appealing.

The Blood Orange Roobios tea wasn't bad, but not nearly as tasty as most other herbal teas I've had. I think I'll pass on this one.

I went to their website to check out their Earl Gray tea, and noticed that it is more than TWICE the price of top-grade Earl Gray that I order directly from Assam, India. That is hilarious. It's clear they make their money on marking up unremarkable tea and selling it to their subscribers on the back end.

I cancelled my subscription immediately.

review_text:
Stay Away, It Is Expensive And Awful. I was so excited for this. I am currently toward the end of writing something I have been working on for three years so I opened this up like it was going to spring forth some golden light and writing fairies were going to come out handing me pens and stickers and little trinkets that I had never thought of.

But I got some hot chocolate. I can’t eat chocolate or sugar. So that was a waste.

I got some really ugly fabric thumbtacks from the couture collection. I like the idea. But these bright orange and black, crayola blue with halloween orange triangles all on a tiny pin for me to post on a wall of my work is never going to happen. They belong in a remainder pile somewhere. Oh wait, maybe that’s where they found them!

And then I got a coaster that looks like a record player but says, when you read it around in a circle “Replaying my thoughts and plots- Scribbler”. Not a bad idea but the coaster is made from a weird material. It feels awkward. I wouldn’t trust my hot drinks on this thing,

Then there was a small booklet that gave some help on writing. I quite liked that. It had some very good ideas.

There is an a button that says, “Ask Me About My Novel.” I have not yet become that pretentious. Nor do I ever plan too. And if I did, it wouldn’t be with a teal and bright yellow pin.

And lastly a book and a nametag with the writers name. It isn’t even written in the book. Quite odd.

If I was shown this beforehand and asked how much I would pay for it, my answer would be nothing. No thank you. I am not sure whether to try again or if this is truly what this has to offer. If so, I am horribly disappointed and would tell you to save your money.

That was my review for November and then lo and behold, I get another box for December even though I was sure I cancelled it. When I contacted the seller, they said they couldn’t accept returns because there is food in the box. So that is why you are getting that random child sized raise box this month!

And a fairly unattractive duo tone tote bag saying “Between the pages is a lovely place to be” with an open book and some black trees on it. Behind that there is a golden mountain in the background with lines flashing out like when kids draw a sun on pictures. Looks more like a warning than a welcoming picture. Again you can make these at zazzle or many places online. (worth $3.95 or less)

Then there is a twenty one page notebook about cliffhangers including an interview with the book writer and nine pages of dos and donts. For example, DO have compelling characters. DON’T drone on and on with description and a paragraph describing why. Felt a little pedantic to me but was probably just the format of the do’s and dont’s in capital letters and the simplicity of the message. But maybe it will be right on for some people. Who knows? The interview is fairly decent but can that information be found easily online by searching writing and cliffhangers basically.

The one pamphlet I did like was the “Inside Look” into the publishing process where they shared Charlie N. Holmberg’s story pitch for “Spellbreaker.”. That was interesting and helpful to read. All two and a half pages of it.

So, all in all I paid $41.50 ($39 plus tax) for what I could have gotten for $10.95 minus the three pages about on story pitch. But if you don’t have Kindle Unlimited like me and have to pay full price for the book, it would cost you $20.94. It’s reasonable to assume you could get the paperback for cheaper than $10.99 though.

Anyway, beyond just the cost of this was the excitement and wonder as had for this that was lost. I bought the November box as a birthday present for myself for my 47th birthday. It was beyond disappointing and I am always very unhappy when the sellers won’t even try to work with you especially when they send articles I am allergic too.

I have taken a picture so you can see for yourself. I want you to know what you are getting yourself into before you buy. Maybe you will love this! And then that will be great. Good on you.

But if it isn’t what you expected like me and if spending almost fifty dollars is a lot of money for you and something you try to spend cautiously then this box is not what you want to spend it on. Many blessings everyone!

Culinary Paint-by-Numbers. I received a 4-month subscription to Blissful Bakes as a birthday gift. To say I was disappointed when the first box arrived is an understatement. Thankfully, my friends were able to cancel the remaining subscription through Amazon. So, what’s my problem with the product?

First: Pricing. The first month’s subscription is $25.00; subsequent months are $30.00. Yet the box I received contained less than $2.00 worth of ingredients. The box pictured online is artfully arranged with craft crinkle paper. The box I received showed no such care. The individual ingredients were stored in baggies, dumped into a box, and shipped.

Second: Quality of the recipes. This month’s offering is Lemon Oatmeal Crumb Bars. We all recognize that a good recipe has value. However, the recipe provided isn’t a Blissful Bakes proprietary recipe, but one that can be found all over the internet. It failed to meet my expectations given the price-point.

Third: Food safety. Flour, oats, and sugar each stored in generic kitchen baggies? Seriously? Under what conditions are these ingredients measured and dispensed? Do they use a certified kitchen? Has their staff taken food safety classes? The manner in which these ingredients are offered up is worrisome. I’m not comfortable using anything provided other than the can of sweetened condensed milk.

Fourth: The premise. You’re provided with the dry/shelf stable ingredients, and a basic and widely available internet recipe. You still have to provide your own butter, eggs, etc. You make the dessert and clean up afterwards. Save your money. Give Blissful Bakes a pass.

I have weird hair, it's thick and wavy/slightly curly, but has a second texture, a very kinky/wirey curl mixed in. These two types have a very hard time finding a pattern together. No one in my family has hair like mine, so as a kid I was on my own to figure out how to style it. I got teased a lot in school because it was so frizzy. Back in the day, before there were luxury hair and skin and cosmetic products in every major box store, products for hair like mine were hard to find. In middle school I started shopping in the "black hair" section (seriously, why is there a separate section?) and found products like Let's Jam (lol!) )worked for my texture. So that's what I used for years. Because of that I figured I would be able to use at least some of the items included.

So to get to it, THE PRODUCTS:
I received. 4 Palmer's Cocoa & Biotin hair products. Shampoo, conditioner, leave in conditioner, and glaxe serum (totaling about $25 value) No mineral oil, no silicones, they make my hair feel soft and strong and shiny and help hold it's curl pattern with no stiffness or crunch. And they smell unbelievably good.
Next there was a travel atomizer of Michel Germain Paris Sexúal perfume, which I looooove (value $30).
Next was a container of Specific Beauty Dark Spot Lightening skin pads that I already am obsessing over. (90 count, very generous, $60 value, seriously). Kojic acid and bearberry, the ingredients are great.

review_text:
OK depending on what you’re looking for. TL;DR: the comics you get are NOT worth double the price as claimed by the seller but the subscription is fairly priced after considering costs involved in shipping and curating comics. Cheaper alternatives include TPBs and subscriptions from the publisher.

What I asked for: Daredevil, Batman, Superman

What I got: 2 outstanding Daredevil comics, #3 of 5 from a random Batman miniseries, a dollar bin Superman comic (Action Comics #999), the rest were B- and C- list comics including a comic that literally said “free” because it was a free comic book day issue.

Shipping: comics are not individually bagged and boarded but rather stacked together and shrink wrapped. As a result there is a minimum amount of creasing around the corners and spine, not enough to affect aesthetic appeal but collectors know even the smallest imperfections can have a significant impact on a comic’s value.

Value: based on previous sales on eBay, the comics I received were worth ~$14. I consider the subscription to be a fair price after considering the costs involved in shipping and having someone curate the comics for you, but by no measure (cover price or market value) were the comics worth “double the subscription cost” as claimed by comic garage.

Alternatives: if you want to read good comic stories, TPBs are among the cheapest way to do so. If you want comics with your favorite characters mailed to you monthly in an ongoing series, you can subscribe to ~12-18 different comic series direct from Marvel or DC for the price of a Comic’s Garage subscription over the course of the year. If you want to be surprised by a collection of random comics each month, Comics Garage might be for you.

Changing my rating to one star. Edited to add on July 7, 2019:
Subscription cancelled and I am reducing my 4 star rating to one star because I went to their website and looked at the cost of each of the chews sold separately and the total cost would be $15.72 plus flat rate shipping $7, so total cost would be $22.72. The first box was a good price and being able to try a variety of their chews was nice, but seeing how they could be bought separately for less than the $29.99 it would cost each month, the subscription box is not at all a good value.

Original review:
They advertise 7 different types of chews per box, and 7-15 total chews per box. I am now assuming looking at the card insert and photo in the product description that boxes for large dogs cost more because some of the chews are larger and it is assumed they’ll consume more chews each month so they get more per box.

I ordered the small size box for dogs under 20 lbs, and did receive 7 different types of treats (all 7 of the varieties shown for small dogs on the card the sent, see pic), and a total of 9 treats (see pics... they came in 3 bags... two of the bags had 3 different types of chews and the third bag contained the 2 large pig skins).

They appear to be high quality chews and my 2 dogs went nuts at the smell of the box, they knew it was something for them as I opened the box and tried to take the first pic! Because we received 2 pig skins I gave them each one and because they were so large I planned on taking them away after a few minutes so they could enjoy them over several days (I usually do with that large chews)... and about 3 minutes later they had each already devoured half of their chew! Apparently they love those chews so much they are whining about having them taken away (sorry, pups... but those are too large for you to gobble up in a matter of minutes)! I should mention my dogs are both about 2 years old and 12-15 lbs... one’s a Scottie/Yorkie, the other a chi/dox... both with long narrow mouths, and neither have been aggressive chewers... but they went nuts for those pig skins like I’ve never seen before!

That said... I am cancelling our subscription because 5 of the kinds of chews we only received one chew (pig skins and beef esophagus strap 2 each)... but with 2 dogs I need to give them each the same thing or they’ll want whatever the other has. Also, the chews are rather large for our dogs’ small mouths, the puff braid is supposed to be small size but it’s so large they’d have a hard time chewing it (they’d probably try... but possibly it’d harm a small mouth... I may give that chew away to a friend’s larger dog). Yes, larger chews can last several days, but I don’t want them eating a large chew all at once and then when I take their chews away I always feel guilty.

I possibly would not be cancelling our subscription if there were double the number of chews that were half the sizes for smaller dogs. 5 stars for the flavor of the pig skins (only thing they’ve tried so far, will lower the rating if they really dislike a different chew), but I’d rate 3 1/2 stars overall for my dogs as I don’t feel the larger sizes of the most of the chews are appropriate for a dog under 20 lbs.

Funko seems to not care, Amazon is clueless. But the items are still exclusive and Pops!. Funko is not listening to their fans, and they’ve basically washed their hands and say it’s all Amazon now. With regards to the huge debacle that was the Dagobah box, Amazon has no clue how the subscription works as evidenced by numerous posts regarding this. I reached out to Funko, and received the below response.

Funko Support (Funko)
Mar 4, 2:47 PM PST

Hi Richard,

I understand your frustration with the Amazon subscriptions. Unfortunately, we cannot assist with orders through Amazon, since they are an independent distributor. We know that Amazon's customer support encompasses the countless number of products they offer, so individual agents may not have in-depth knowledge of how their company processes these subscriptions.

If supplies are limited, that is a concern that Amazon must handle with their distributor contact or supply chain management, so it is disappointing to hear that they are pointing you to us, when we handle issues related to purchases made through the Funko Shop.

And while we do not have any insight into Amazon's system, our best guess is that next month's box is shown on Amazon's website, leading their customers to believe that they will not receive the current month's box, or that there is a delay in shipment. For example, a February box expected to ship in April or May.

For further support with your subscription account, we encourage you to reach back out to Amazon and see if they can put you in contact with a representative that has more insight into their Smugglers Bounty boxes.

Best regards,
Maca with Funko Support

Now...with regards to content, well...it has gone down. I’ve been a subscriber to Smugglers Bounty since it’s introduction when it was done directly by Funko. So I have tons of pins and patches, t-shirts or hats, even socks and wrist bands etc. The box quality has declined, we used to get art specific to the theme on the box, now it’s just not the same.

Specific to the “Dagobah” theme now: SPOILERS!

A movie moment...okay, these aren’t always popular, they’re large and hard to display. Especially if you have to look down to see them. I’m not usually disappointed in them, but I was this time mostly because we literally just got a movie moment from “Empire” when we got the Cloud City box. So to receive another movie moment was disappointing. The mystery mini HAD to be who it was or else we wouldn’t have gotten him at all. So many things they could’ve done with Yoda!

Overall the box isn’t the same as when Funko distributes the box themselves. We haven’t had a wearable since Amazon took over. I really wish Funko would listen/read the reviews and see what fans are missing and wanting. I personally love Star Wars, and I do enjoy having exclusive items you can’t find in stores. So I keep buying, but the dollar doesn’t always stretch as much as it used to.

review_text: Very Impressed. I was very tempted by this subscription box based on the description that Amazon provided. Hair accessories work hard - they get in the sun, they get a ton of oils and products on them, they move with every step and beat around in boxes full of other metal, plastic, and stone items. If you're lucky, they last a long time and look good doing it. That part remains to be seen, as I have only just gotten my subscription and have only worn everything once or twice. review_text:
Decent box as long as you aren't expecting too much.... Pros:
1. Really cute themes every month
2. Good variety of toys (nylon, rubber, etc) and you can customize how much of each kind you get by
contacting customer service. You can also customize to have a "toys only" box if you aren't interested in
treats
3. Great customer service in general
4. Good price for the number and quality of toys

Cons:
1. Hard nylon toys should ONLY be given to puppies - that way if they crack a tooth it isn't a permanent one.
As a general rule of thumb, if you can't make at least a small indent with your fingernail, it is too hard for
adult teeth. They really shouldn't be encouraging people to give rock-hard nylon toys to adult dogs.
2. If you have a dog that is over 75 lbs then this is not the box for you. The toys in the "large" size box were
on the small side for my GSD and are a full-on choking hazard for my mastiff. They should have an option
for giant breeds or they should explicitly state that when they ask you for your dog's breed, that they
aren't actually using that to choose the toy size - every dog in the large size box gets the same toys
regardless of whether they are a 60 lb collie or a 200 pound mastiff. It's extremely misleading for them to
ask what breed you have and then send everyone the same size toys anyway.
3. Their rubber toys are not nearly as heavy duty as kong or bullymake rubber toys. For true super chewers I
would choose bullymake. I have both subscriptions and I find that while barkbox is okay for my GSD, the
toys they provide are entirely unsafe, and not nearly durable enough, for my mastiff.

Conclusion:
I will keep getting this box for a couple of months because it has a nice selection of toys for my GSD and my smaller mixed-breed. However, they really should be offering a size up from the large box - I would say the toys in the large box would be more accurately described as being for medium-sized dogs like collies, smaller labs, and spaniels. The attached picture is of the rubber toy they sent after approximately 10 minutes with my mastiff (who isn't even full grown yet). The tail was ripped off by my GSD about 20 minutes after I took this picture. The whole things was in the garbage after about 45 minutes when I caught my mastiff eating pieces of the rubber. However, I will say that my experience with customer service was great and they sent out a replacement toy immediately, so no complaints there.

review_text:
Great way to passively introduce coding and math. If you have an advanced 1st grader this is about the perfect amount of challenge for them to tackle. The box requires young learners to learn the keyboard and lessor used keys which is a skill learned much later. It gets students used to x/y axis, functions, if/then, critical thinking (if you do the challenge), creativity, and a good preview of how code is written. These skills are all way early so the box doesn’t need to explain what a function is or go into detail about how x represents the horizontal movement. It shows them and now they have a concrete example in their heads for when they are shown the maths behind it.
My learner quickly caught on, adjusting the first value would move the stamp left or right.
The best part is that after we did a section he wanted to make his own without the guides.
This is an almost perfect box. The only downside here is that the introduction just ends. It doesn’t say begin card # 1 or anything. It just ends. Also 2 apps on the first kit don’t have a card. They are hidden on the tricks and tips card. So they need to redo the directions and intro but certainly keep the part where you throw the kids right into coding. It’s something they will pick up by doing.

review_text:
SUPER hit or miss. Every time.. Some of the stuff is really cool and practical! So far in my boxes, I've got a SandBar, a waterproof bluetooth speaker, some nice (women's) tank tops. Resistance bands! Books on squat technique! A handy fanny-pack type thing!

Some of it, I can't figure out. Why did I get a box of ginger tea & a container of tequila-lime seasoning this month?? What does that have to do with fitness?

Some of it is just random stuff with a brand name. LVFT fleece headbands -- yes, I can get the exact same thing at the literal dollar store, with no brand. So far, I have received two. Yet I only have one head.

But the problem for me is the stuff I get that I would never, ever ask for. Examples:

I am a vegetarian, but I keep getting boxes with beef jerky sticks. No option in my profile to mention dietary preferences; which is one thing for me, but what about people with food intolerances (they send peanut butter!) or religious restrictions??

Another example: I don't appreciate the pandering to me, as a female, with fancy smelly sprays and scented wipes and "face refreshing spray" -- seriously? I want what the guys got (you often get different items if your box is for male or female). And maybe the guys wanted the fancy smelly wipes. But Gainz doesn't ask, they just assume. Why did I get whey powder this month and the guys got pre-workout?? Huh???

I think the last straw was getting a unisex tshirt (from Hybrid Performance). In the account profile, you specify not just size but, as I mentioned, also gender, so that you can get the fit you want. Are you a girl who likes longer, looser tshirts? Go with a guys size. Are you a guy who wants flowy tank tops? You can choose a girls size. So WHY are we getting unisex anything? We pay a premium to get premium cuts, not the run-of-the-mill cuts. And, I did a little digging -- Hybrid Performance DOES make women's cut shirts...just not the one Gainz Box sent. Hmm.

My subscription is halted until I can see spoilers in time to decide each month if I actually want what they're sending anymore. Going in blind is only worth it if you can use a BOGO code -- look for those on social media -- that way, if only half the stuff in each box is good, at least you got a full box worth of good stuff. :)

review_text:
Cosmetic Formulation Chemist: half thrown away every month.. Their products are a mixed bag of poor formulas and dried out products. I’ve subscribed since their first box (2014?) and the quality has gone from 50% potential for allure beauty award and 50% start-up/ new launch, to 90% products that were likely given to them for free and 10% new launches.

The last box, when the price hike started, included a vitamin C (LAA) powder that the ‘editor’ claimed could ‘be added into your daily moisturizer’ (so does the company). Of course it isn’t done BG anything to your skin, because it’s NOT DOING ANYTHING FOR YOUR SKIN. first I’m a cosmetic formulation chemist, and that’s not how to make an efficacious L-Ascorbic Acid formula:

LAA is EXTREMELY pH dependent, even if your DRY formula contained a manically powder pH buffer, you cannot accurately dose out 2-3 ‘shakes’ to make an effective serum, not to mention adding it to moisturizer (FOR THE LOVE OF SCIENCE DO NOT DO THIS). This is beyond stupid, it’s potentially dangerous and Allure is backing this; If Amazon rejects this review because of this, they are too.

Anyone who has a problem with properly formulated LAA serums, please try Vitamin C’s other forms: magnesium ascorbyl phosphate, Ascorbyl Tetraisopalmitate, sodium ascorbyl palmitate, ascorbyl glucoside, 3-0-Ethyl Ascorbate and a few others that can be stable and effective in a properly formulated moisturizer.

I believe (although I could be wrong), the sachet dish that came in this box is an extra item that comes only in the first box.
The 5 teas in bags, contained only 2 tea bags each for a total, including the sample, of 11 tea bags and a small tin of tea. The first cup with a tea bag took quite awhile (longer than the recommended 3-5 minutes) to get a even a fair amount of color and flavor of tea, into the water. I tried re-using the tea bags, as stated in the description (2-3 cups per bag) with very little success. The second (I wouldn't even dare try a third) cup of tea, I let each bag steep overnight, and never did get even close to the first cups' amount of tea into the water. In other words....I was only able to get one satisfactory cup of tea out of each tea bag. Now as I previously stated, I have tried just about every tea subscription out there and I ALWAYS reuse my teas to make two, three and sometimes even four cups each time but I was not able to get even close to that, out of these teas. Granted, I have only tried three of the teas in one monthly box but, in terms of the tea alone, I certainly didn't feel like I had gotten my moneys worth.
This sub seems to be about more than just the tea itself though and if you are in it for the extra(s) as much as the tea itself, you may find it to be worth your money. Though it just wasn't for me.
Thank you for your time. Hope you are well.

review_text: Everyone has an opinion-Don't let others make up your mind for you.. I have heard and read many reviews upset over the first run of the collector's corps through Amazon.  I was a member of collector's core for about year with Funko before it switched to Amazon.  Is it different now? Yes. Are there items found in the Funko version missing from the Amazon version? Yes. Should you subscribe anyway? Depends on you.  For me I am happy with the FIRST box.  These boxes are a suprise each time and filled with items that I cannot or usally would not find in my normal day to day shopping experience.  I am a collector like many others who subscribe. I focus mainly on Marvel legends figures and have Pop! as a side collection. I enjoy the idea that each box will have a custom one of a kind Pop! in each box. I like knowing that I have something in my collection( as small as it is approx. 50 or less Pop figures) that others cannot have without a subscription.  So to me I enjoy the suprise and the value of this subscription. I don't see this as a way to beat the system and circumvent capitalism. These boxes cannot be sold at  a loss and continue. There must be some sort of profit. Otherwise the toys and collectables we all love will cease to exist. So I do feel that this is a good value and something to look forward to every other month. I encourage you to try it and see for yourself. Some months are far better than others (my bruce banner/Hulk two in one Pop! being one of my all time favorites) but overall they are fun to collect.  Besides if you get something in the box you don't like or enjoy give to a child in your life.  They tend to be much less picky about toys than the adults posting here.
