review_text:
Initial impression wasn't good, but the seller is making things right. After seeing a video online for this service, I decided to give it a try. I just received my first box, but it was underwhelming. This is what I received:

Standard PC AC cable
Molex to SATA power adapter cable
80GB SATA 1 hard drive
PCI based modem card
Excelius retractable cleaning brush

The parts were packaged well and included a handwritten manifest of the parts that were given.

I realize it is a mystery box and what you get will be different every month and different than what someone else gets, but the claim that every box contains $55 or more of parts is not accurate based on my first box. At best I’d say $15 tops. The only item of any value is the hard drive, but at only 80GB and SATA 1 it is only good for use with older systems and laptops...fine for Windows XP or 7. That’s really about a $10 used part based on prices on the bay. The rest of the parts I got were “meh”. The cleaning brush is nice but I’m sure it costed them maybe $1 each to have a bulk order of them purchased with their company name put on them. I’ll see what comes in the next box a month from now as I want to see if it is going to be crap again or if it will have some better parts worth more than what I paid. So far, not even close. I like the thrill of a mystery box, but it better live up to claim that there’s $55 or more in value. I’ll update my review either way to help those of you wondering if this is a good deal or not.

UPDATE 2020-01-27: I reported the problem to the seller, and I was contacted almost immediately after that. The seller gave me a partial refund. He explained that I should have received much better items than I did and that for my next box he would personally ensure I receive items that meet what is promised in the product description. I bumped up one star for great customer service. I will review again after I received my next box.

UPDATE 2020-02-27: The box I received was better in February. There was a functional 500GB SATA hard drive, a Chromebook (parts only), an Excelius wallet tool (very cool), and HP rechargeable laptop battery, and an HP motherboard. The motherboard has some bent cpu socket pins, but I might be able to repair it. I'm not sure what I can do with the battery and Chromebook, but at least the LCD of the Chromebook looks like it may be working. I will report-out again in March on the quality of that box.

UPDATE 2022-03-29: Boxes got really good for the most part over a year. Then the box I received Feb 2022 had nothing but junk...literally maybe $10 worth of parts. There was no list of parts as there normally is, and the box did not have the Excelius label on it. Then a week ago my subscription was canceled. I did not initiate canceling it either. The service was great IMO this past year...not sure what the heck is going on now, but I'm not happy now.

Bit of a letdown. I hunted for a subscription box service for my honeschooled 9 year old that would give him some screen free entertainment and learning outside of our usual routine. I watched several youtube videos of several STEM boxes before deciding to purchase this one, primarily sold on it based on the fact that it was discounted, and I felt it was a low-risk way to see how we felt about it before committing to a full year.

The box arrived ahead of schedule, which was exciting, but was already smaller than anticipated, because all of the unboxing videos and advertisements showed this kit coming in a durable tin lunchbox style case, and advertised that the first box would include a canvas bag... not a huge let down, but misleading and also detracts from the overall calue of the contents.

Upon opening the box, my kid and I were both underwhelmed. Included was a booklet describing the contents, the "Who Was" series book about Frank Lloyd Wright, a black and white postcard, which was ripped on one edge, 3 Wonder Crate Heroes cards, and a sample of a construction toy kit that was simple cardboard shapes and plastic clips. I paid $22 (at a discount) , and recieved a $6 book, $1 worth of trading cards, a 50c postcard and what amounts to at most, a $3 craft kit.

I will not be continuing my subscription.

review_text:
Clever way to learn programming. Bitsbox is a clever, well-designed program to teach an actual programming language. We stopped our subscription after the 4th installment and have no regrets for trying it out.

What We Like About Bitsbox:
* Kids are learning a programming language with real-world applicability
* Beautifully designed materials delivered in a box that lights up our kids' eyes when it shows up
* Step-by-step instructions about how to develop each app
* A unique QR code technique to transfer an app from a web browser to a mobile device
* Includes extra material for parents, encouraging engagement together

Concerns:
* Having to use a text-based editor instead of a visual programming interface is, in our opinion, a limitation. If a child has good typing skills, this is less of a deal--and it might not be a problem for you. I've just seen how they engage longer in visual programming environments. And if they're preparing for something like Mindstorms, learning in a visual environment with blocks is a helpful thing to get used to.
* There are other ways to learn programming that are free. Personally, I think Bitsbox is a little overpriced for the value in comparison to other options. However, there are a couple different pricing options on the website that we didn't catch onto when we started.

Our bottom-line:
Our 9 year old prefers MIT's Scratch. It has a visual programming interface, it's fun, and you can take someone else's program and "see inside it", which is to say "you can learn from their code". You can re-mix someone else's program, which is an interesting learning technique. And she enjoys the community aspect of Scratch.

Our 7 year old prefers Bitsbox! Despite his just typing in what he's seeing in the code provided, he enjoys the games and when we work together on Bitsbox projects, I think he's picking up on some little things.

Where Bitsbox shines is the step-by-step learning process, which is not nearly as strong with Scratch. If you don't mind the Bitsbox subscription fee, do both! The key is that the kids ultimately find that programming is fun and engaging.

UPDATE: My 7 year old wanted to jump back into Bitsbox this week. We started tweaking a game and came across a coding issue we couldn't solve. I sent a support email to Bitsbox and literally less than 5 minutes, someone got back to us with a clarifying question. We answered the question, she reviewed the code, and replied promptly explaining the issue in a way we could understand, with an offer for further help. So impressive! I'll suggest that's why Bitsbox may be worth paying for. Good job, Bitsbox! I wish I could share the name of the person who provided the great support but I'm pretty sure it's against Review policy guidelines. But thank you!
product_name: Bitsbox - Coding Subscription Box for Kids Ages 6-12

review_text:
Treat yourself!. After having flowers for nearly two months (birthday and anniversary are a few weeks apart), I missed the splash of life in my dreary windowless office when the last of them died. As with anything else, I headed to Amazon to look for a solution. Bloomsybox looked like the perfect match and was offering a discount. I purchased a three month subscription and received my first bouquet a couple of weeks later.

Despite being in the middle of a winter storm with sub zero temperatures, the flowers arrived in excellent condition, with just some bruised guard petals on the roses. I was impressed with the mix of varieties and colors. While the roses started to die a few days later, the rest of the bouquet held up well. Every few days I trimmed the stems, changed the water and removed any dying material. It was nearly four weeks later before I finally threw away the last of the greenery.

My second bouquet arrived on time and in even better condition than the first. The roses in this arrangement lasted a solid two weeks before they started to droop and three weeks before enough had died that I threw it away. The photo is this second bouquet at two weeks old.

My third bouquet was scheduled to be delivered over our Christmas holiday but Bloomsybox let me delay the delivery so I’ll be receiving it after I return to work.

While it may be a bit of an indulgence, I’ve loved having fresh flowers in my house office and plan to continue to treat myself periodically. I would unequivocally recommend it as a gift to any flower lover in your life.

I only have one minor complaint. The description and their website say you’ll get care information with the flowers and I didn’t. While it was easy enough to look up the flower varieties and care online, it was a little annoying to expect to have it included and then not get it.
product_name: Beautiful Bouquets Subscription: Mixed Flowers

I'm a fan of the idea but not the execution. I purchased the discounted first month of one of these boxes (the February 2020 Cupid's box) to try out. I agree with others that $24 a month is a lot for what you get, but I would be willing to look past this, factoring in not just the items you receive, but the amount of time you'd have to invest in putting something similar together.

However...

In two of the three recipes, we had to make significant adjustments. Not just for taste preference (way too much salt called for in one), but for practical purposes. As an example... the muffin recipe that came with this was the consistency of wallpaper paste 'as is'. Had to add liquid to thin it down enough to be able to add the chocolate chips and raspberries (which would have been a total mess to try to mix in otherwise). So for me, if the recipes can't be used as written, what's the point?

I did agree to give this one more shot, so time will tell.

Also on the negative side... not only do you not receive the apron by going to Amazon route, you don't have a way to create an account on the Raddish Kids site. It just seems like this could have been better thought out.

review_text:
Survived my terrible terrors - good quality for the cost. [[VIDEOID:fe0c4c07f36943a946ffd89ec196329b]] (In short, good toys, I’m happy with them, though I can imagine a few cats not being as interested as mine are.)

As someone who fosters a lot of cats (and has a couple long-term residents), I figured getting toys every month would be nice if only to send them home with the fosters when they go to their new furever families. $20 for 4-5 toys isn’t too bad considering good quality toys at a pet store usually cost around that much. So I went on over to the KitNipBox site and subscribed, asking them to replace any treats with another toy (since cats can be pretty picky about food sometimes, and one of my residents has a sensitive stomach).

The toys are purrfect - the theme this month was the beach and (although I had my hopes set pretty low just in case) I was impressed and quite happy with everything. Each of the four adult cats currently in my home seemed to take a liking to a different toy. One of my resident cat loves crinkle toys and started happily beating up the yellow beach towel as soon as I gave it to her, and the other wouldn’t leave the jingling sandal alone (she has always had a love for bell toys). And my current fosters (two terrors who have torn apart countless mice and other toys within minutes of receiving them since I started looking after them) instantly took a liking to the toys that were stuffed with catnip. I was worried they would start ripping them up and eating them like the other toys I’ve gotten for them in the past; they were chewing on these ones before I even took the tags off! But I was worried for nothing - they have been chewing on and beating them around for the past couple of hours and aside from being soaked in saliva, they’re still in pretty good condition (which is more than I can say for the dollar store and Walmart ones I’ve gotten them in the past). The ‘dietary box’ replacement toy (that one foster is carrying around in the video) even matches the theme of the box, which is a nice surprise.

Will definitely stay subscribed to the box myself! Though if you’re thinking of getting this for your own cats or as a gift for cats of a friend, please take their personalities into consideration. My cats love new things and cycling through playing with their old toys. They also love all kinds of treats - hard, soft, freeze-dried, any flavor (though they don’t have to clean their boxes when the one’s stomach reacts poorly to it). Not all cats like to run around and play with new toys, and some are picky about treats - if mine were less enthusiastic about playing, I probably would have cancelled the box (or wouldn’t have ordered it in the first place).

They can’t tolerate moist soil beyond their watering day as it will cause the stalk to wither and consequently the succulent will die.
Each type/variety is unique for its leaf shape, color, texture and personality, if you believe plants have such a thing. It’s going to be exciting, my monthly anxiousness, to discover new varieties when the box is opened.
Speaking of boxes, each plant was individually and carefully wrapped in bubble wrap and arrived safe and healthy. I like the monthly program even if they are 1-2$ higher than your local retailer. Magic school bus engineering lab - some pretty complex experiments for my son, more advanced than Pre-K. Each experiment has a one time use, so if you mess it up, you have to replace the supplies. Most of these supplies are general household or School needs. The solar generator was the best, and reusable.

Code and go robot mouse - this was and continues to be my son's favorite. He and his friend spent hours programing the mouse, though rarely used any of the prefabricated designs. Great for inspiration, creativity and adaptability.

Gizmo's building set - offered neat designs and ideas. We haven't spent much time with this set, but my son picked it up and built many creations on his own with little to no interaction or guidance from me.

Robotics pet 600 - more complex building than Gizmo's, though offers creativity and adaptability. My son was able to follow the directions with some guidance. It's like an early Lego Technics set. Caution-its fun to let it walk off the table and explode.

Probably going to take some time off, play with current sets and resume in a few months. Worth it, though.

Expensive for what you get. I canceled this subscription today. There are a lot of mazes and puzzles which my son does love to do.
I had these set up as auto payments then today(we are half way through the 50 states) and i get an invoice in the mail to pay them their $20.60. It auto pay but they decided to not do that anymore and have me reset it up. Then i sat down and asked my self is this magazine worth $10?
No. In total to get all 50 states that costs $500 over the course of about 2 years to get all 50 states.
There are way better educational and fun things you can purchase for your child for that kind of money. Think of all the family passes you or museums you could go to for that $500. It really is a ridiculous price for what you get. A laminated name tag and magazine. If your kids really truly love it and you find it is a wise investment go for it. My son will be 7 soon and he would much rather go to museums and see actual exhibits. You can check out books about any state and attraction at your local library and watch online tours of state parks, monuments etc if you are unable to go yourself. Those are much more interactive in my opinion than these puzzles(though puzzles are great for brains). Purchase puzzle books for a few dollars or purchase state themed/natural wonders/monument themed jigsaw puzzles or board games to make learning about states fun and family oriented. There are way better and cheaper resources out there folks.

The project took maybe 10min and she hung the final project on our Christmas tree

An unspoken benefit is that we now have plenty of colored pencils and glue! We add the extra supplies to our art box and break them out regularly.

I really hope this subscription is varied enough to continue for at least a year. I love that each activity is built for two. The little kids love it; my 13yr old niece loved the tye dye activity (she stepped in once the littles were done); and I love it too

My Thrill Club is not thrilling AT ALL!. *Second Review: February 3rd, 2021*
Okay....so, I recently received the second box from My Thrill Club. I was a bit apprehensive when opening it because the first box I received was pretty much a dud.
Well....... same goes for this one!!!. It was LAME!
I have never heard of the 2 hardback books I received. Plus, one of the books was from a series. They didn’t send me the first book in the series though.... Oh, no no no..... they sent me the 2nd book..... a flippin’ sequel!?!?! A sequel in a book series I’ve never even heard of!
I have a book account on Instagram, and so, I went and asked other readers who have subscribed or purchased a box from My Thrill Club and what their thoughts were on the boxes they received. Nearly all of the readers that I asked had the same feelings that had: we were unimpressed with My Thrill Club.
This was a gift from my lovely sister-in-law. It was an AWESOME idea for a gift, I just wish her money was wasted on a company like My Thrill Club.
I only have 1 more box coming my way, so, I’ll be writing an update after it arrives.

*First Review: December 30th, 2020*
My awesome sis-in-law got me a 3 month Subscription for Christmas and I was super excited about it. Well....I just received my first My Thrill Club box, and so far, I’m not that impressed. I’ve subscribed to quite a few Bookish Box subscriptions before and My Thrill Club is my least favorite. Like the website described, I received two hardback books, Hunger & Vampire stories. Thankfully, I’m happy about one of the books I received...even though I’ve read it before. I really liked the book but I had borrowed it from the library.... so now I have my own copy to add to my book collection. Other than the two hardbacks, the website also described that there would be an ebook, or a code to a selection of ebooks? I got no code. Which, after reading several other reviews, I’m not the only one missing the part of the subscription that was described. Bummer.
Will I be recommending this box to friends....I don’t know. We’ll see how it goes after I receive the next two boxes.
Huge thanks to my sister-in-law for the thoughtful gift. She did an awesome job...too bad My Thrill Club did not.

review_text:
There’s 2 sides to this company-and I’ll tell u about both..... Ok, I’ve had over bcA year of dealing with this subscription company-and I’d like to share a. Review from two viewpoints-the subscription department end & the product end of it.

Subscription department: I’ve had a subscription for over a year now, SOMETIMES TWO! How? Bc at one point they somehow started another one with my card information-( I think it was bc I tried to prepay for 3 months at a time.) One month I even got 3 BAGS!!! I had referred my mom to the club & at the time the reward they were offering was a free bag,-instead if adding a month on my pre-paid account-they just sent an additional bag for that month! So I got 3 bags of lip stuff I ended up not using!! Since it was a prepaid gift card, I wasn’t too freaked about canceling it & became amused at what exactly they were going to try to keep pulling with it as long as they were allowed. When they kept trying to charge me for a 3 month subscription I DID try to find where & how to cancel it, but it’s not obvious. I finally decided to just send it to their customer care department and it wasn’t ever acknowledged. As a subscription company I feel their customer service is non-existent. Unless you are subscribing you won’t easily find anyone to help you.

PRODUCT REVIEW: see subscription review! No I know I need to be more clear-there were a few good products that I got from them? But overall it’s a complete miss. I’m not the first to say this! The colors are either brown or bright pink or orange, and I keep getting repeats sometimes as soon as the month after! Plus it’s NOT 5 FULL SIZE products, it may be one with a full chapstick and some deluxe samples...or the lip pencil they send doesn’t match the lip color that they sent...and they love orange! I’m not kidding I thought it was a colored pencil it was so weirdly bright orange!! Orange! Not coral. I wish I had kept all of them I would have posted a pic of them...if I ever come across one that I didn’t just toss, I’ll post a pic.
Now you might say it’s bc I’m not hip on today’s colors, but I have 2 teen daughters,17 & 16, and uh nope! I can’t push it off on them either!
Oh and the flimsy pouches they send the product in? Boo!! (I guess I’m spoiled by Ipsy!)

So overall-please don't get mixed up with this company! Don’t even just try them for a month bc it’s a total waste of money. Instead just go out and buy one nice tube of your fave shade-AND USE IT! You will be 20 times ahead of all of us that wasted $$$$. Plus really-how many shades do you wear?

The average gal barely gets time to throw her face on, before she runs out the door to start her day anyways! So if you get the time to put on actual lipstick, you might as well wear what you really love right?!

****By the way, if you want to have a fun experience ithe a beauty subscription, get the glam bag or plus from IPSY...AS OF TODAY DO NOT GET THE Ultimate Glam Bag from them, they just don’t have their act together with it yet? But I’ve been a subscriber from almost their beginning & they are always there if there’s a problem, and I get two regular bags & a plus every month. Plus they have super discounted specials on different products everyday. Love them.

I was really hoping for a Pop! Rides Yoda Riding Luke! Not a disturbing dead-eyed head. My Dagobah themed box was delivered today and the only item I like is the cute Yoda "mystery" mini. It's not really a mystery if there is only one design included in all these boxes.
As for the "Dagobah Face-Off" movie moment, I really hope it grows on me. Honestly, since I saw this "movie moment" in the actual movie in a theater when I was a kid, its image has disturbingly haunted my memory for many decades.
It's not exactly a wholesome scene, in fact it's a horrific experience for Luke. Who wouldn't freak out after seeing your own dead-eyed disembodied head in a scary cave. And now...it's been memorialized in physical form...by way of a Funko Pop Star Wars movie moment that I now possess.
I was really hoping the Dagobah box would contain a "Pop! Rides Yoda Riding Luke Skywalker". I would have loved that and I think that would have appealed to a broader audience as well. Another movie moment idea...Yoda Raising Luke's Ship Out of the Swamp.
Anyway...the sticker and the sticky note pad are meh at best. A total of 4 items. None all that thrilling. Definitely not worth the $30.00 plus tax I paid with my hard earned money. Why can't they lower the price of this subscription box to $20.00 each since that's closer to total value of what they contain.
Sad to say but the reason I'm continuing my subscription is "for fear of missing out!" And I'm not even a millennial!

review_text:
Should have had a better, bigger & more exciting Pop. Just another variant of the many common Venom Pops.. This is my first subscription box and I hope the next box is better than this Venom themed one.

There are so many Venom Pops (both old and several more recent ones) that look alike. If this box contained a bigger or a more unusual Venom Pop then it would have left more collectors like myself happy.

The Venom t-shirt is barely okay and could be improved in terms of the quality of the material used. Doesn't seem like this t-shirt is going to last a long time. It's a simple design on a cheap t-shirt.

Instead of the stress ball, tiny venom figure & sticker, I would have preferred something more useful...like a key chain, luggage tag, pen, etc.

All in all, the contents of this box isn't worth close to $30 + tax. And at this point, the only way for the Marvel Collector Corps Box is up. I'll continue my subscription until the next box. If it doesn't improve, then I'll be cancelling.

review_text:
Just received the second of the same kit in 4 months. Wazzup Amazon?. I purchased the STEM Club for my grandson who is just turning 5. 5 is a problematic age ... just beginning reading readiness for most kids so they may have trouble with reading some of the STEM vocabulary. I am sure that it is difficult for Amazon to come up with items for this age, Pre-K. I have a bright but not precocious grandson, A lot of things which do not require reading seem to be too simple for him or, if reading is required, he has trouble with some of the vocabulary. I read the reviews for the first kit, the "Young Scientist Club The Magic School Bus Engineering Lab". Frankly the kit was disappointing because some things worked, some things didn't and the whole thing was "cheesy". Thin cardboard, poorly thought out sequences of "experiments" and the like. His mom suggested I save my money, or give him a $20 bill. I said we would give it a second chance and we are glad I/we did. The second unit was the "Learning Resources Code & Go Robot Mouse Activity Set" which was a (stored program) robotic mouse with a travel platform (durable), some instructions (which we read and figured out together), cards which were an aid to figuring out the steps for the program, barriers and pictures with which to build obstacle courses and a magnetic wedge of cheese. Eli mastered the entire thing in under a half hour. He knew the mouse was a robot and the objective was to find the cheese, but he got the grasp of programming the mouse without considering the steps as "programming", he was just telling the mouse what to do. He showed off his new skill to his his mom, dad and grandma when they each arrived. I was excited to watch him learn. It provided for great conversation/discussion. This one was a hit. We are all looking forward to the next kit.
The Gears! Gears! Gears kit we received in July was a hit, but we were all disappointed to receive the second Young Scientist Club The Magic School Bus Engineering Lab kit in 4 months. We hated it the first time, please don't send it again.
product_name: STEM Club Toy Subscription: 5-7 year olds

review_text: Had Barkbox for 2yrs. Stopped cause….. As stated I’ve had bark box for 2 years. The different themed ideas every month is cute, but honestly my dog could care less. I feel that’s more of the owner’s appeal. Initially, my dog enjoyed every bit of bark boxes, he started knowing what the box smell or shape was and got very excited when it was delivered. I would cut the box open and let him drag things out himself. After nearly a year he started playing with the toys less and less. I can see why, the toys were always stuffed with squeakers in the middle. There are options to change toy types, but those are more costly and I’d much rather get the exact toy type he likes at the pet store that’s going to last a lot longer. The treats were very helpful in finding out his likes and dislikes. I appreciate the variety they had, as did my dog. Now, after 2 years my dog just lets his toys pile up, he started giving them away to friends lol since there’s a mountain of them. The only thing I would get from barkbox is treats and I didn’t see the worth In that when I’ve learned my dog’s preferences. So I decided to cancel. I cancelled the annual subscription and auto renewal by online chat. My account even showed cancelled. THIS IS WHERE IT GETS STRANGE. Come time for my usual renewal, it charges me…I reached out in confusion, tried looking for a confirmation email-that didn’t exist. THEY DO NOT PROVIDE CANCELLATION CONFIRMATION. I even asked for one and they said they don’t do that. YOU MUST MAKE EVIDENCE FOR YOURSELF (screenshots, etc.). Cause they might try to charge you again. The agent was professional and did still give me my full refund without problem after trying to get me to stay. But I refused to continue the subscription. Hope people see this so they don’t think they’re crazy, when they clearly did cancel. Once I’ve gotten my refund back, I’ll be deleting my card info and account if possible. We had a good run Bark Box, thank you for everything.

If it were a better value, I could take the unknown random choice, but these are basically albums that regularly sell at a standard discount at around $25 being sold at $25. I'm assuming they are trying to move overstock, so why not give the subscriber a deal we can truly appreciate as an incentive? $15 iseems like a decent price for getting quality overstock records.

Charging us $25 for a $25 record... when you could instead buy a different one of your specific choice at the same price... doesn't make sense.

Fun, Worth the Money!. My review differs slightly from some of the others here. I have a pretty extensive record collection and Amazon still finds releases I value and wish to add to my collection. If you're reading to figure out what kind of albums you'll get, here is what they've sent me so far: Miles Davis Bitches Brew, Pink Floyd Dark Side of the Moon, The Clash London Calling, The Who Sell Out and and Simon & Garfunkel Concert in Central Park. Most of these are 2xLP releases and come from recent high quality (and desirable!) represses. Sure, everybody has "Dark Side," but now I have a copy I can take the posters out of and put stickers that stick on stuff - not to mention an audiophile pressing of the album!
People going off about these albums costing less than their subscription fee: Sweet! Cancel your order for that month and go buy it there! This comes to your door and if there's a problem customer service will take care of you. People also going off about not being able to cancel in time if they don't want it - that is on you! Amazon drops it in your cart every month between 22nd and 30th and won't ship until at LEAST the first of the month. If you can't check your cart at least one of these days - as said - that's on you!
I like this service. I have a pretty big record collection but I never bought any of these "classic" releases they've sent me because the vinyl gatekeepers often have original pressings priced much higher than they are worth (especially with this uptick in the last 20 years) and the re-presses are often a similar story.
If you want to relive the Columbia House days of 10 albums for a dollar and their inferior materials and pressings I do suggest you keep digging in the bins - the very same ones I will be digging through as well - to find your copies of the classics.

review_text:
Why ask if you don't intend to listen?. I purchased the DC subscription for my son when this went on an Amazon discount. I expected a hodgepodge of whatever. But then I received the following email from the vendor:

Thank you so much for your order. Along with your selection of Marvel, DC or both we would like to know what characters you would like included in your Comic Garage box as well. While we cannot guarantee every character, we do have most and will curate your box around your selections.

I thought this was awesome and very proactive on their part. And even though they stated that nothing was guaranteed, I figured that since my son only likes Batman & Joker and the Flash, it should be doable. So I reply exactly that:

Thank you for taking the time to see what I would like!
This subscription is actually for my son. He loves anything Batman & Joker and Flash.

So, they subscription arrives a few days later and what do we get? No Flash. No Joker. 2 Batman. And a crap ton of Superman (which my son hates), obscure titles and a really raunchy, pornesque comic that I will not be giving to my child!
I completely get that you want to get rid of comics that aren't selling at other venues and you also want to introduce people to lesser known titles, I do. My issue is why bother asking what someone is interested in only to send everything but? I think I am more disappointed with the selection received because of being ignored. It wasn't like I requested 10 or 20 different characters. And when you're told this is for a child, don't send porn! Needless to say I canceled the subscription and went to B & N and bought Batman/Joker & the Flash. I wanted to love this. I wanted to surprise him every month with 24 new comics. But it wasn't meant to be.
product_name: The Comic Garage Super Box

Eh. Only get it if there is a sale!. I have wanted to try this subscription service for so long. I love trying new toys and treats with my spoiled baby girl. I just could never bring myself to pay the price. So when they were having a sale on the subscription box, I couldn’t help myself. The box came very quick, I was actually shocked how quick. I was excited to open it up with my cat. But to be honest, the contents were a bit lackluster. I got the box for multiple cats. It included five or so cat nip toys, all the same. Most were the same brand and a brand I’ve seen at many retail box stores. My cat was excited to open the box up, but she didn’t take to any of the toys as much as she usually does. As for treats, it came with cat wine! I was really excited to receive this because it was another item on my bucket list to try with her. Other than that, it was okay for the 15 dollars I spent on it. But I would never pay 30 dollars for it. I don’t think it would be worth it and you could find cute toys at a local pet store. I could have received a dud box, but I would still not recommend it. It’s quite a lot of money for what you get.

EDIT: I live in a small town with only a few stores and one pet store, that’s why I wanted to try this out so badly. But today I went to a discount store and found two of the items I received for 3.99. It’s fine because I paid 15 dollars for the multiple cat edition. review_text:
Really great box..but...BEWARE of the treats if you have kitties with diet issues!!!!!!!!!!. This box is great! My cat absolutely LOVES the toys that come in it! So far we have received two boxes. The first box was a safari themed box and it had some really neat things in it...about 4-5 toys and a little food/treat. The treat in the first box was a salmon flavored type of liquid/juice. We tried to give it to your kitty but she completely ignored it. Ended up throwing it away because she didn't give it any attention what-so-ever. The second box was full of a bunch of red colored toys...one was a heart, another was a cute pillow with a feather...general stuff like that. Really awesome! BUT...it was the treat in the box that was bad...

So, the treat in the second box really caused our kitty to have an adverse reaction. They were organic dental treats that did not go so well with our kitty. We gave her the recommended serving (like 3-5 treats) and all was well. The next day, our kitty came down with the WORST constipation and gas ever! It was so bad we had to bring her to the vet. They ended up helping her pass her issues with some fluids/medication. Suffice it to say, we have discontinued this package and picked up the toy-only package instead!!

As a side note, our kitty is 11 years old and she has had some dietary issues in the past...so, that can be a contributing factor...which is why I am NOT holding the company/service accountable for her issues at all. However, please keep this in mind if you have a cat(s) that have had diet issues in the past...you might want to rethink the package with the treats!!

Aside from that...absolutely LOVE this package and it is a great way to introduce a variety of toys!

My box included a "martini glass", an extremely short wand toy, and three similar rectangular objects: a "suitcase," a "book," and a pretend powdered drink mix "envelope." The martini glass was the only item my cat showed any interest in, so I'm guessing it was the only catnipped toy. The stick end of the plastic wand toy has a very sharp extra piece of plastic sticking out that I will have to remove before trying to entertain my kitty with it again.

Maybe some months are better than others, but the offerings from this particular month just didn't appeal to me or my cat.

review_text:
Disappointed Human, Happy Cat. I got this on sale price, because I wanted to trial it before committing to a full price subscription. I've seen so many advertisements for KitNip in the past year and I was really looking forward to trying it. I read the reviews before ordering and was surprised by the negative ones, but I figured if it was on sale, it would be worth it.
My cat got three small fabric toys, a bag of treats, and a wand.
The wand's handle is very short. It's uncomfortable to hold it when the actual fabric portion of the wand is about the same length as the plastic handle. My cat really loves wands, so he was pleased. Me and my partner, not so much. We prefer to use his other wands that we've bought.
The treats were freeze dried bison liver. My cat is very picky, so he didn't like them. No biggy. I tried my other cat who isn't as picky and he didn't care for them too much. The dogs though? They eat everything and wanted the treats for themselves. It's a small bag that I can purchase individually on Chewy for under $5.
The fabric toys consisted of a plain Martini shaped one, which my partner says looks like a UFO. It's not the most appealing design. My cat loves fabric toys but this is his least favorite. Again, the dog likes it more. The other two fabric toys have crinkle and a bell sound to them, so my cat prefers those more, especially since their shape and form is better than the martini one for him.
The toys weren't a wow factor for us. They seemed mass produced and cheaply made. They list the values for each item on a cardstock insert. But honestly, everything felt Dollar Store like. Nothing against Dollar Store toys. I've bought my cat toys from the Dollar Store before but if I'm paying a subscription price, I expect a bit more or better quality. Overall, if you can afford the full price every month and love your cat, it would be worth it. But if you'd rather just buy your cat toys yourself, then maybe skip on the subscription service.
product_name: KitNipBox | Happy Cat Box | Monthly Cat Subscription Boxes Fi...

review_text:
Kind of Lame. The materials that come with the box are top notch. If you are just looking for an interactive version Clue, this is it.

If you were hoping for something with psychological, factual depth, and social intrigue, YOU WILL BE DISAPPOINTED. The actual crime story and content is super lame. Like, Scooby-Doo type lame. Every suspect is one dimensional, at best. Also, no one is likable. Everyone is egotistical, vapid, overly dramatic.

Our most recent episode features the supposition that one character poisoned a horse to death with an accidental overdose of 5mg of Diazepam. REALLY? No one could be bothered to look up the maximum dosing for horse anesthetic? Okay, maybe some of you don’t care about that.

The suspects are the only people who provide statements. No one else offers any information. The witnesses do not answer any questions. They offer a few cheesy paragraphs of “oh I am so amazing. By the way, this death is so tragic. Gosh I wish I could be more helpful.” They do not share any information about their relationships with the victim. They don't really share any information about the other suspects relationship with the victim. They don’t even share town gossip.

This town is so small it apparently does not have a grocery store. However, it does have a bar, restaurant, veterinary hospital, pharmacy, record store and school. Oh. And it takes everyone at least 30 to 40 minutes to travel 1 to 4 miles from one destination to the other.

If you like details. If you enjoy feeling connected to a mystery, don’t waste your money.

It’s a great concept. Bummer that they spend such a small amount of time on plot and character development. They need to pair down their graphics design budget and hire a couple of fiction writers.
product_name: Hunt A Killer

- getting 2 they already sent (but to be fair i got 45x3= 135 dvds from them so far)
- last month i got the dvd knockaround guys, but about 20-30 mins in it kept freezing and skipping so unfortunately that one isnt any good (but still not their fault and it was bound to happen).
All in all i highly recommend if you are looking to add to your collection w/o paying much per movie (less than $1). I truly believe i will order again, but due to lack of space may have to stop sooner than i would like

* got my 2nd box (2nd month in a row that i ordered). Kept my genre selections about the same as im mostly doing this to have a bigger variety of kidmovies. Chose 40 pacl, got about 43 or 44 dvds. THE COMPANY DID NOT SEND ME ANY REPEATS! SO THATS A HUGE PLUS. I would say 4-6 dvds we already owned, around 3 or 4 i previously owned (but had given away to make more space at the time). Several i had heard of before but didnt recall seeing (but these titles were supposed to be good). About 75% of the box was family friendly for all ages while 25% or even less was geared more towards older teens and adults, but that's ok with me because i was mostly trying to find things for my toddlers and if there was something myself or my teen liked then thats cool too.
*1st review-Ordered 40 dvd pack. Chose genres: kids 2-6, family, action/adventure, comedy, edu/doc/musical, suspense/thrllr, scifi/superhero, drama. *I swore I had narrowed down my genre options to 4 or 5 a couple days before it shipped. Maybe I didnt save it right or it was too late b/c they were already selected?* estimated arrival was feb 22. Well they came today feb 8! My box had 45 dvds instead of 40 s0 that was nice. review_text:
Not cool Facetory...Update. Update: I received my Summer 2022 box a few weeks ago and I was surprised to find all items were repeats I had recently received in the last couple of boxes, so I thought it was just a mixup. When I messaged Facetory about it, they told me this season's box was a "greatest hits" theme of items subscribers requested to see again.
So we negotiated a 20% discount and I kept the box. I appreciated their willingness to accommodate. Now here's what I don't appreciate.... Why am I now seeing the REAL summer box on social media?? I mean WTH Facetory, you flat out lied to me! The real summer box had the Facetory products along with 7 masks and the booklet was back. So, why didnt I get what I subscribed to? I just dont understand this business practice and am truly disappointed. I loved this subscription even with its little issues. But, I just can't continue it. Thanks for the fun surprises and introducing me to new Korean brands but I will now go back to being my own curator. (See new photo of Summer box. Looks almost the same as the pic of my winter box. Sheet masks not pictured but they were also repeats.)

Just got my winter box but wondering why only 4 products? Subscription is for 5-6 full size products so I feel a bit ripped off. I've been getting these boxes for a year now and while I love most of the items included it seems Facetory doesn't really go by the season when choosing products. I mean this box includes cleansing foam and a cleansing balm. 2 cleansers in one box, for winter?? Not to mention cleansers are the cheapest product of any line. So was this box worth the $49.95 price tag? I don't kniw because this one didn't contain the product booklet they usually include.
Then there was a toning mist and peeling pads another two items that they've sent in almost every box so they could've passed on for this box. And NO moisturizer! This is rather disappointing. I tend to use products according to how my skin behaves during the year. Now, I will have to store a couple items again for use during the the appropriate season. The summer box also contained a really greasy massage/cleansing cream that I had to put away until the weather got cooler and my skin felt drier and needs more heavier creams.
Facetory should send everyone their fifth product. I've never received a box with 6 full size items so I don't know why they even put that in their ad. To cut the box short with no explanation and no price difference just seems crooked.

review_text: CLASSY, TASTY AND FUN BUT NOT INEXPENSIVE. I waited until I received one year's worth (four) Classic Bokksus to write my review.  First, regarding the quality; the boxes, accompanying literature, and the wrappers of each individual item in the boxes are striking.  The boxes themselves are refined and as solid as paper boxes can be.  I never received a damaged box or box with damaged contents.  Not a single item ever arrived stale.  I receive an email from Japan every few months notifying me that someone has mailed something to my address.  I'm not 100% sure but these might be the Bokksus because they seem to arrive shortly thereafter.  Everyone who saw the booklets commented on how beautiful the photographs were.  As to the contents, there's a good variety of sweet and savory in each box.  I like the little cakes and pastries the most, followed by the different types of tea.  I'm not as enamored with the hard candies that often leaves me feeling that I'm sucking on a sugar ball colored with artificial dyes.  I guess I expected more punch with natural flavors.  As several others have noted, the cost is rather high for a box full of snack items one might find on the impulse buying racks at a checkout lane at a convenience store.  Having lived in Japan before, I can say that while they taste good, some of the items, especially the salty snacks are pretty inexpensive to purchase there.  Taking into account the cost of shipping from Japan and the need for profit margin however, I suppose this is understandable.  I find myself having a hard time keeping up with the arrival of the next box.  That is, a new one arrives before I've finished the previous one.  This would make an outstanding gift subscription for someone interested in Japanese food/culture.
product_name: Bokksu - Authentic Japanese Snack & Candy Subscription: Class...

The box came with very little, so if you don't know plants or how to care for them, you are on your own. This is not a box for someone who is bad with plants.

One of the pairs, the polka-dot plants (no names or information about the plants was provided), were wilted and weak-looking right out of the box. I tried my best to save them - proper sunlight and watering regimen, etc - but they both died within a week and a half anyway. I think they were too far gone by the time they got to me, as nothing I tried brought them back.

The other pair of plants was far heartier and are doing fine, but I also could have gotten a similar pair from the corner shop for about half the price.

Exactly what it says. Well, it's exactly as the description says, an essential album every month. Whatever Amazon decides is essential. I really only like a couple songs on both albums I've received, but they have both been classic or essential albums.

I enjoy my other vinyl subscription more as I get more eclectic and interesting vinyls, but this is building out my collection at a good value.

I just like what I like when it comes to music, whatever moves me and makes me feel, old or new. My wife is the opposite though, she's more into what was popular during certain time periods, usually the 70's / 90's and stuff, Tool, Nirvana, AC/DC or whatever. She picks on my taste in music frequently lol.
She enjoys listening to music that's "good" and I just like listening to music for the feels :D

I think this subscription would be good for someone who's looking to build out their collection with "good & popular" essential music albums.

As for myself, I'll stay subscribed for now, as I am enjoying receiving new (to me) music I wouldn't normally tune into, expanding my horizons.

Value is questionable.. So I got 18 pieces total. One was thinner than a pencil. The two I gave my pups so far did not last long at all. (Labradors).

Natrual chews go for 1-4 dollars in general. So let's say average of $2 a piece. For having 18 chews in the box at $2 a piece, that is $36. If there were only 15 chews (minimum amount they promised), you would just break even if each item was an average of $2. Now consider you can buy things like pig ears in bulk for less than $1.50 a piece. What I am trying to say is, I think the value of this box is just okay at best. It seems like you might break even.

What really buys me is they source in South America. Which, if you didn't know, South American cattle farms are causing a lot of deforstation. It's very profitable for them to cut down the Amazon and other forests and create a cattle ranch. While the farmers/ranch hands/cattle might be treated well, this does not mean it isn't causing a ton of enviormental destruction by supporting them. Obviously I cancled my subscription.

Smells great and brings joy - packaging could be less clunky. My boyfriend got me a 3-month gift package for this and at first I was so mad because it is never something I would ever buy for myself! But after using the Fall box for a few days, I all but fell in love. The rose gold oil and pumpkin whipped soap smell so good and I always make it a point to use when I shower! I hope they last me a while (I tend to use very little product so things last me a while). I received my 2nd box today (Lunar) and some of the products seem pretty cool, like a toner and a primer/moisturizer combo, there's a lot of products to wash my face this time.

The only thing I found slightly annoying is the huge amount of shredded paper in the packaging. I just want to see the products when I open the box, I don't like to have to get rid of all the paper first!

Also, all the packages come with a little motivational workbook (one month it was an internet detox book and this month it is a notebook about manifesting your values, etc). I haven't had the time to use them and just based on my personality it seems unlikely that I will. So I guess if you're not super into that, it could be a waste of money. The products are nice though. I don't know if I would ever pay the full price for the products that they list in the booklet (it seems like I could find some cheaper alternatives that do similar things) but I like them so far.

review_text:
Fun Ways to Learn About Each Other. My wife and I subscribed to this box on a whim, and it has been one of the best purchases we've made in a long time. So far we've gotten two boxes, one arcade themed and the other shark themed. Both were high quality and absolutely packed with fun activities. The types of games varied greatly from card games to board games, truth or dare, and even a small shooting gallery that had to be set up in a hallway!

While some of the games are just for fun, others are designed to help you get to know your partner a little better. After the shark themed date night box, I now know my wife has no fear of clowns but is scared of heights. We've been together for years, yet I never knew this, and these are the little things that draw couples closer. Other games encouraged you to talk about the past or to even open up some relationship secrets (i.e. "What's the worst thing that your partner has made for you?"). The questions and prompts never got too serious, which I've noticed is a complaint for some earlier boxes.

One of the best things about both of the boxes we've received is that there are more date activities than are used in the prompts. The arcade box included a deck of cards that had different date ideas on them; the prompt only used the cards, but never the ideas. They were a complete extra. The value for the money spent is incredible. We were hesitant to try Crated With Love out at $30 a month, but after one box we could tell that we were getting far more for our money than many other $30 date ideas.

We look forward to future boxes!
product_name: Crated with Love

review_text:
The Gift That Keeps Giving. I gifted this subscription to my husband last Christmas, thinking we would only subscribe for a few months after reading some reviews that said all the boxes start to look the same after a while. Yes, every box has a tie and a pair of socks and often, a pocket square (not always), but there are five items in each box. Each box has a theme - a person who inspired it. You have to read the accompanying booklet to find out who it is if you can't guess. The first photo I uploaded is the most recent box, "American Rocker," which was styled after Lenny Kravitz. I also uploaded photos of my other favorites: "Rocketman" (Elton John), and "The Duke of Cambridge," (Prince William). The other photos show most of the contents of the eight boxes my husband has received so far. He has loved every box.

The cool thing about subscription boxes is that they give you the chance to try things you wouldn't normally buy for yourself. This box has really inspired my husband to try different styles, plus he loves getting a surprise each month. A couple of months after we subscribed, the price went up from $25 to $30 per month, but we still feel it is a good deal. The blue watch in Photo #6 arrived with a broken hand a week before we were due to move. I contacted the company's customer service, and they not only replied right away, they rushed us a replacement so we had it before we moved. They were awesome!

I cannot recommend this subscription enough. I think it may be the best gift I've ever gotten my husband (and I've gotten him some pretty cool gifts).

Cons: The toys are tiny cheap crap, basically all made in China, and half were unsafe to leave with the cats unsupervised. Summary: purchase only if you need $20 of instagram props for a monthly cat photo. Half will probably be uninteresting to the cat after 5min, and the other half will have to be confiscated for safety.

review_text: Perfect for a budding foodie/chef/home cook!. I was worried about a kid's cooking subscription being too young for my eager 11 year old who already has some decent skills (she makes pumpkin and meringue pies from scratch easily, etc) as most kid's cooking books are lacking real skills and variety but adult cook books may be too complex or sophisticated for a learner. Nope! This is perfect for a more serious kid or even casually learning some life cooking skills for any age. It might be a little pricey for some for what it includes, but the way the recipes are adapted to make self-teaching, or semi-self teaching easy is perfect for busy parents or parents that may not have a lot of from-scratch or varied cooking skills themselves and worth the price. The recipes have illustrations for the steps and are laminated and include information about the foods, the country of focus, and similar dishes from around the world making it educational beyond cooking. The recipes expand the palate without being too daunting to try. In my experience, one of the best ways to get kids to try new foods is by them being involved heavily in cooking it. This is perfect for that! It would be easy to cater the child's involvement for each recipe to the needs and skills of the individual. The ingredients are easy to find and the list not too long. Last night it was from scratch ravioli and tiramisu, with an antipasto recipe we haven't tried yet. This would be a perfect option for homeschooling especially as the kid(s) can be involved in the shopping where math and reading can be utilized, and naturally math is part of cooking as well as physics and chemistry. Glad I have it a try!

review_text:
Not worth it -- even on sale. Signed up during the late 2018 subscription box sale. Even with a cheaper first box, this was a regretful waste of money. The candies are worse than grocery store bulk bin selections for a frankly ridiculous price.

Sour box in general: Terribly misleading lies. Only 1/7 was described as sour. Another was "sweet & tart". The rest were all sweet. I'll run through all 7 (6 plus a bonus) in the November 2018 box:

Dorval Sour Power Strawberry/Apple Belts: This was the only content described as sour. Sour Patch Kids are more sour. The belts themselves were unappetizing and stiff. If you blindfolded me, I never could have guessed the flavor.

Arway Christmas Tree Pretzel: The pretzels were stale, soggy, or both. Mush coated in flavorless white chocolate.

Gerrit's Strawberry Licorice Wheels: Ridiculously bad licorice or nearly palatable wax? I honestly couldn't tell.

Arway Dark Chocolate Holiday Nonpareils: Generic dollar store dark chocolate that manages to make Hersheys look gourmet by comparison, managing to be both bitter and chalky.

Vidal Gummi Christmas Trees: "Sweet-tart" in the same way a tangerine is sour. The gummi texture was passable. The flavor was mild, which was deeply disappointing as one of two remotely sour items in the "Mostly Sour" box.

Albanese Gummi Snow Flakes: The one completely acceptable item in the box, with a texture similar to a Haribo shark and reasonable flavors.

Bonus -- Sweet's Peppermint Salt Water Taffy: As I eat this, I picture a tourist trap beach town. Not the taffy spun in the window at the fancy candy store. This is the taffy down the street, in between the airbrushed t-shirts, ironic snow globes with melted snowmen, sunscreen, and cheap sunglasses.

Even on sale, I feel ripped off and regret not heeding the other 1* reviews. Please don't make my mistake.

Nothing Like Expected! Super Lame and Not Worth the Price!. I didn’t order this through Amazon, but through the Lip Monthly website, and let me tell you... it was AWFUL!

I got two different lip glosses that were basically the exact same color and didn’t work with my skin tone, a clear chapstick from an independent company based out of Oregon (that one, I at least liked for supporting an indie brand, but it was still pretty dull for a lip subscription bag), and a black eyeliner... the bag was one of those cheap drawstring bags from China.

Still, I gave them another chance thinking maybe I signed up too late for the previous month and that was what was left.

A similar thing happened the following month, but at full price. Almost every color was the same and I was unimpressed... at least that month I got a cute zip pouch?

I went to cancel because the lackluster appeal of this subscription, but they gave me an incentive to stay by offering my next month at around $7, so I gave them one more chance.

I already have an Ipsy subscription I get for a variety of makeup products. I just wanted lip products through Lip Monthly (crazy concept, I know). It also would have been nice to have some kind of questionnaire to customize bags to customers based on skin tones, skin type and product preferences (ie, like liquid lip or lipstick, matte or glossy, moisturizing, spf, etc...).

Save the money on this garbage and go to the 99 cent store or Walmart and pick your own products you actually like and will use.

This subscription is a joke and a money grab, pass on it.

review_text:
Boxes full of miniature snacks for fairies, not people!. I received the 25 snack box for the first time and was not impressed, the box came 1/4 filled, and the other 3/4 was empty space, what a ripoff for $40 per month. Everything was super tiny, I could fit several items in the palm of my hand. The snacks included 3 little bags of pretzels, various kinds of jerky, lots of energy bars, and two little bags of random chips. These things seem like stuff they couldn't sell at a grocery store and they just packed it up in box to resell for unsuspecting customers. I appreciate that the snacks are healthy but I think I can definitely get more worth of my $40 buying it from a supermarket, personally. Maybe if the cost of the subscription box was halved I would continue my subscription, but at the current price, it's best to look elsewhere for snack boxes.

I forgot to cancel my subscription so I got a second box, still full of the same little tiny pretzels, energy bars, and jerky. At least this time I got a small bag of cookies...It feels like this company really loves their pretzels, I have so many pretzels now instead of a variety of chips or crisps, how disappointing. To inform how little you're actually getting, I had combined both snack boxes together and there is still space for probably a third box of snacks. If the original box included twice the amount of snacks it had, it would be a better deal, and I would feel like it was worth getting, despite the lack in variety of snacks. As for the taste, I tried about seven snacks and they were OK, but not anything impressive, since they are basically your everyday snacks you could buy from a grocery in mini form.

Update:
SnackNation offered to provide some additional snacks for no cost for me to try due to me being unhappy with my previous boxes, and I accepted. They shipped me two mini boxes, which were completely stuffed to the brim (unlike my giant box of mostly empty air), but I can't say if this would be true for subscribers for their newer boxes, so I would reserve my judgement on this until I try a full sized box from them.

The new snacks they gave me were surprisingly bigger than what they had given me in the past, and again, I do not know if these changes will be reflected in their new boxes, but they had promised me they were changing their curations for future boxes, so I hope this is true for the sake of their subscribers. They included a variety of snacks which I hadn't seen before, and I would say I was happier with this selection that I received for free vs. the selection I had gotten when I paid for the subscription, but this might be due to the changes they were making to their boxes as they had mentioned to me. The snacks are still on the smaller side, but not so much as before, where you felt you got cheated somehow by the tininess of everything. I would say the new snacks are appropriately snack-sized for human beings to consume now, instead of for tiny fairies. But they also included some duplicate snacks between the two mini boxes I received, which could be either a bonus or a con, depending on whether the snack in question tastes good or not.

For example, they put the same bag of RIND snack in both boxes, and unfortunately, I have to say this snack is one of the most unpleasant things I have ever placed in my mouth. I've only gotten through half of the first bag and I will question my sanity if I try to attempt to finish the second one. I appreciate the RIND company for trying to come up with healthy snacks, but their versions of dried fruits is absolutely disgusting. The fruits included were dried pineapple, dried kiwi, and dried orange with the peel on. On the back of the snack bag, it encourages you to eat the peel since it contains a lot of nutrients, even more than the fleshy part of the fruit. So I tried to heed their advice and put the whole dried orange in my mouth, peel and all, and chewed it for three seconds and had to spit it back out. It was the most bitter thing I had ever tasted in my life, and I've had tried many bitter things before, but not to this extent. The dried kiwi was like dried extremely sour ??? covered with a very light coating of sweetness which was wholly unpleasant. Only the dried pineapple was passable, but honestly, it tasted like a vampire sucked all the juice out, chewed it a couple times, then spat it into the snack bag for us mere humans to finish.

However, the other snacks I have tried have been great so far, and I will post further updates as I go through my snack boxes. I am still undecided whether to restart my subscription, but perhaps I will give them another chance in the future if my finances allow. For now, I would bump my rating to 2.5 stars.
product_name: SnackNation - Ultra-Premium Healthy Office Snack Box Subscrip...

review_text:
Good Combination. The coffees are good and do show a nice variety. If you go by the standardized cup markings on the side of most coffee pots, I got about 18 "cups" out of each packet. It would probably be about half that number in coffee mugs. I use about a scoop for every two "cups" I make. If you like your coffee stronger, you'll get less out of packet. Despite the fact that they are pre-ground, I don't have any complaints about freshness. The bags are sealed at least as well as any commercial pre-ground coffee and are (according to the company) freshly ground a few days before you receive them.

Update: when this review was written, you got 2 packets, each with a different coffee per month and each packet made 18 "cups". A matched cookie was included for each packet. Now, you get 1 packet per month that makes about 36 "cups" and two cookies of the same type. It's the same amount of stuff you got before. But, the single larger quantity match may be more convenient for sharing.

The cookies are very good for a packaged cookie and have an interesting combination of ingredients, making them a bit more unique than a simple chocolate chip or sugar cookie. They seem to be a fresh baked cookie that is sealed in a plastic wrapper and then shipped. By the time they get to you, they have dried out a little, but they are still very good. As for size, they're just a little bit smaller than the rim of a plain white coffee mug. That's not huge, but it's more than adequate.

My only complaint is that it took a full 2 weeks after the date that Amazon placed the order for the package to arrive. For a company that seems to be trying to ship a fresh product, that's a little slow. I'm not sure how much this is impacting the freshness, but it is a concern.

Note that MY order date was even earlier. Amazon places the orders once a month, which means your order is also delayed until about the 14th of the month. I'm not complaining about because it doesn't affect the freshness of the product. (I gather it's made fresh AFTER the Amazon order is placed.) You DO have to be very aware of the total time frame if you're planning to make a gift of this, though.
product_name: Match Made Coffee - Organic Coffee & Gourmet Cookie Subscript...

For whatever reason Amazon does the following:
A) Lists this as a digital order (which causes confusion with the Non English speaking reps)
B) Will not allow you to use gift cards on this and says that its because Funko made that rule (seems like funko didnt).
C) Does not process the orders by who had the subscription the longest (i.e. I know one reddit user placed his order a full week after me and already has tracking info).

I will update this once Amazon fixes these problems. I love Marvel and Funko and this is NOT a slight to them in anyway shape or form (The boxes are quite awesome in general). review_text: Amazon's Record Club is a Fun Idea that Needs More Work. I was really excited to join this Vinyl-of-the-Month club. As a music lover with a turntable working to build an incredible music collection, it seemed like a good opportunity to get some older albums I might have overlooked. It's focus on albums from the '60s and '70s sounded perfect. I participated for 5 months, but decided to call it quits. My primary issue is that I don't think Amazon has put enough thought into their selections. It started off promising with Credence Clearwater Revival's Greatest Hits, an album by a band I'd heard of but not heard. Then came The Who's The Who Sell Out, again, a band I'd heard of but never listened to. Then things took a bad turn. December's "album" (in quotes because it wasn't one) was Blondie's 12-inch single for "Heart of Glass." While Heart of Glass is a great song, this was a disappointment, since it's a single and not an album. For $25, I felt like I wasn't getting value. Then January and February brought two albums from the same band: Pink Floyd's Dark Side of the Moon and The Wall. Great albums and classics for sure, but getting two albums from the same artist in consecutive months feels like whoever is choosing got lazy. I've now quit the club and will be curating my own list of classic albums to buy.
product_name: Vinyl of the Month Club: The Golden Era

Many of the items have been very clever and done in a way that is tasteful (like recipe cards! not TOO childish to use as an adult in my kitchen ;) and one great quality printed card stock). You WILL get items you may never use, but they make fun gifts that always get a laugh (like a mini pusheen desktop vacuum!) and are still very high quality. For the quality, presentation, variety, and quantity of items in each box, I have to give this 5 stars. Well done.

There is one pitfall I must say - the theme of the box sometimes can be off-season. I know my "fall" box came with Halloween items on November 2nd - I would have loved to have them during Halloween, but I just kept them for next year! Not a huge deal, but if these are "box exclusives" it would be nice to have them come before the holiday they might be themed for.

Also - to address other reviews saying they received the wrong size in apparel and rated it lower due to this - I wanted to say that the customer support of these boxes is amazing! They replace items without a fuss and are always very professional. I wouldn't worry about this at all.

review_text:
The second month is a Photoshop mess placed on a Tshirt.. First off, I love the Streets of new Capenna set. I'm a huge 1920's - 30's buff and appreciate the mobster, speakeasy, industrial, and art deco styles they incorporated. However this product was not something I would have even bought from a bargain bin.

The first month I received was great except they sent me the wrong size. This second month was a huge dissapointment. The material, though soft, seemed stretched. Like someone already wore it stretched. The smell was like dust and ink and not that new t-shirt smell. Also, the shirt stated it was coming in black and came in a navy blue. I feel the color choice was wrong, more on that next.

The image on the front is big and gaudy. Like someone painted it on the side of a van. The picture depicts the 5 mob bosses of New Capenna. I love these characters in the stories and also on Arena. However they don't belong crammed on a shirt. It's easily noticable that these are the exact images from Arena. They are photoshopped onto the chest and become a jumbled mess. The art is blurry, the contrast is flat, the lighting is dark, and the only thing that pops is the gold border and green glow from Jetmir the Cat Demon head of the Cabaretti.

The first month we received an awesome Blue Mana shirt done in the art nouveau style. I'm not a blue player typically but this thing was awesome! However it seems that this is a 50/50 chance to receive something good, so far. I will be getting next months shirt but if it's anything like this I will return it and not order another.

I feel that this particular printing didn't do the artists justice of who originally painted those characters. I believe it cheapened those pieces. Like a shirt you would find on vacation and you only buy to gift it to others.

I'm going to leave this at two stars because I did enjoy the softness of the material. Although loose fitting, the first shipment wasn't like this, it did feel nice.

I’ve tried them all & How To Be A Redhead is the best subscription box!. If you are like me, you’ve tried so many different box subscriptions. I’ve tried everything from Ipsy to fabfitfun, to even smaller subscription comapnies and nothing or no one compares to how amazing How to Be a Redhead’s subscription box is!

Every single month I feel like the box caters to my exact needs. It’s SO REDHEAD FRIENDLY & great for my sensitive skin! They really put a lot of time and effort into thinking about their clients with each item they put in……. It’s very apparent. Plus, the benefit of all of it… is trying new things! I’ve spent thousands over the years trying beauty products from the regular store and end up wasting my money with products that either make me breakout, aren’t right for my skin tone, don’t match my red hair, terrible quality, have horrible chemicals, or a thousand other reasons!
I swear most big beauty companies have never talked to an actual redhead when they make their products…… some of the stuff they come up with is just a joke.

I’ve had my How to Be a Redhead box subscription for a while now and so many of the items I’ve received I’ve loved so much that I buy them on the regular now. Some of the items that How to Be a Redhead make themselves have been in the boxes & those are my favorite boxes! I’m legit obsessed with my redhead Bobby pins…. Show me which box subscription gives out a different color besides the black and brown Bobby pins? My updos have NEVER looked better!

Some of the reviews I’ve read on here are outrageous! I’m sorry, but it’s true! These boxes value is way more than you pay for them, it’s a great deal honestly. Like I said before, I would pay thousands to try a product out and I honestly have saved money getting these boxes and not wasting so much on buying the bigger chain store products that I don’t love. Rarely do I receive something in the box that I don’t love too! A lot of the products are cruelty-free, save on plastics, and don’t have those terrible chemicals in them!

I read one review that said it’s generic products and I couldn’t disagree more. Order from Ipsy one time and you’ll notice what’s generic! 🥴

I haven’t ordered their deluxe box yet, but I’m looking forward to it because if this box is GREAT…..I can only imagine how amazing that one is!

Lastly, I have a few friends with red hair and this subscription is a great gift idea…. Just saying!
God- I could go on and on…. But like you get the point I’m literally obsessed & my favorite time a month is when my red box is at my door.

review_text: Excellent Product. If you have a child who likes to solve mysteries and enjoys learning about history and other cultures, this is perfect for them. My son was hooked right away with the fun letter that explains the mission. We really enjoy the map that was included. This is not a quick activity book, there are so many different activities. We didn't work on it everyday and it took us about a month to complete everything and solve the mysteries which was perfect timing for when we received the next packet.  I am an early elementary teacher and was both pleasantly surprised and am impressed with the variety of activities to complete: search and find, matching, codes, opposites, critical thinking skills, etc. The reading level of the guide book is higher, I would guess about third grade and above, and the activity book would probably be upper second grade or higher. My son was able to read the activity booklet and I would read to him from the Top Secret Guide Book. It was a nice balance for shared reading. So, if you are wondering if this is at the right reading level and interest level for your child, I would say it is good from first grade (with help reading from adult or older sibling) to 5th grade. The older the student, the quicker and more independently they will be able to get through the activities. I highly recommend this.
product_name: Highlights Top Secret Adventures

Disappointed in this Subscription. There is so much great artwork available for Dungeons and Dragons that i thought some of it would appear on the t-shirts. Most of the shirts, including the one that came last week, follow these examples.
Of the last year, there were 4 shirts I would wear regularly and the rest occasionally.
While I might recommend this for the younger gamer, I would not for an adult.
I have cancelled my subscription.
The shirts did come when advertised and there were regular updates when one shirt was "late" by coming on the last day of the month. The are comfortable and washed well.
This subscription had great promise, but very seldom delivered.

review_text:
Good music, bad system. If you like rock from the 60's and 70's, with broad interests in that genre, you'll like the selections. Pink Floyd, Simon and Garfunkel, Hendrix, The Who, Black Sabbath, The Clash, etc. represent recent selections. Also, the price is generally lower than if you just went and bought the album on Amazon (sometimes considerably so). Notice, however, nothing outside rock, despite what the club description might have you to believe. No Motown, Funk, Soul, New Orleans sound, blues, jazz, etc., at least during the year or so I've been a member.

One problem is I already have over 1/2 the albums that they have chosen for selections. Not a big deal in general, but Amazon does not send an order placed email like usual - I only get an 'item has shipped' email. So, I have no chance to see what the selection is and cancel it before the order is locked in a shipping status. That means I am returning an album most months of the year. Not only is this terrible for the environment (e.g., fuel and packaging costs both ways), but it is a hassle to me (and hurts Amazon profits!).

Come on Amazon, give us 24 hours to tell you if we already have the title so we can cut down on the return shipments!
product_name: Vinyl of the Month Club: The Golden Era

Cute but except for the feathers on the toys, may cats had zero interest. I could tell they did not smell any catnip. They were more interested in the box (I believe Meowbox sprays the box with a catnip scent). We received about 5 or 6 toys and the cats walked away. They used to LOVE the toys that were soft and stuffed with catnip but the few stuffed toys we got yesterday, cats had no interest. Sadly, I'll be canceling now. $20 is a lot of money for my cats to care less and I throw it away in a month. I can go buy other toys at specialty shops for that. I wish Meowbox had kept to the small businesses that made super stuffed toys instead of going commercial dollar store like.

I was a little skeptical and will really hold my opinion until I receive my second box. However the first box pleasantly surprised me.

1) You pick the characters you are interested in. My custom box fit pretty well into what I chose, no real deviation.

2) Grades - I would review all 11 comics at ~9.4 NM condition. All are unread and in pristine condition.

3) # of Comics - I received 11 instead of the listed 10

4) Value for money - If you divide the cost of the box by the total items, you pay ~2.70 per issue. Several issues are valued at $30, which includes the Spawn 11.

5) Variety - My box included 1992 prints all the way through 2017. All major titles and several #1 first print covers. a good mix.

If the boxes continue with this mix and quality - it is well worth the subscription price, and easily adds value to your collection.
