review_text:
Ignore the people with no sense of fun. Pusheen Box is great.. I have subscribed to the Pusheen box for a couple of years now. My wife loves Pusheen and every month is a new fun surprise for her. Before you purchase, you have to understand, not every box is an "A+". All of these subscription "mystery boxes" are a little bit .. uneven. Some boxes are "ok that's all cool" and then there are some (like the Fall 2020) that just arrived) that absolutely knock the socks off of the recipient. Fall 2020 was the best box yet.

I will say that the Fall and Winter boxes seem to be the best; I think that is partially because of the nature of the season. In Fall and Winter, you tend to get something warm and fuzzy like a hoodie or a blanket, etc. The Spring and Summer boxes are always good too but think about it.. They can't exactly send you a Pusheen bikini (sizing that for the general public would be impossible), so spring and summer tend to be more display items.

For $50, every month I get to see my wife light up like a kid again with fun little trinkets, clothes, blankets, shoes, you name it. I hope they keep going with this for years to come.

review_text: Great product. Why are y'all so grumpy with the reviews.... I do have some drawing/doodling ability, but I have trouble coming up with ideas for new things so I decided to subscribe to Artsnacks. I received quality art products in complementary colors. I got to try new types of art supplies, and more importantly, I got some boundaries to play in. I had these certain colors, and these types of supplies, and I just had to make something cool with them. So, I did. For all of the reviewers complaining about the cost of the products and stating that you could have found an item cheaper on sale somewhere: why don't you go and do that? You goal is to find the cheapest value, so maybe you would be happier searching online for a price that suits you. I have found the prices that Artsnacks lists to be in the range for what the item sells for. For those of you complaining about the randomness of the supplies: that's the point. You should subscribe to this if you want to try new (art) things. Anyway. I liked my items. I made a silly drawing. It made me laugh. I got to try a Copic marker. Was fun, but I think I liked the cheaper KingArt color brush pens much more than the Copic marker. The lead pencil was great, and Stabilo markers are always cool, but I use them for writing, so using them for art was new. So, maybe you should give it a try.

review_text:
So-so first box, hoping it improves. I was a founder with the original MCC box when Funko was producing it, so I haven't missed a box yet. Now that Amazon has taken it over, I am optimistic that the box will get better. For those that are unfamiliar with the MCC Box, when Funko started it, each box was unique and had comic print on the inside of the box that corresponded with the box theme. The box also contained a contents card so you knew what was in the box, a pin, a patch, an exclusive variant cover comic, a shirt (or on rare occasions a hat), an exclusive Pop figure and several smaller Funko items.

With that being said, let's start off with the POSITIVES about the Deadpool box ....the Pop figure was nice and unique, and the luggage tag was nice. The NUETRALS are the taco truck 2 taco holder and the fairly unimpressive generic box. It is a different item that I never would have thought to sought out on my own. The NEGATIVES are the Pop keychain (not impressed), the lack of a contents card listing the items that are contained within the box, no exclusive variant cover comic, no wearable item, no pin, and no patch. I will stay subscribed at this point to see where Amazon goes with this, but if the quality of items doesn't increase....there are other things I can, AND WILL, spend my money on.

review_text:
Bookshelf Lottery Ticket. If you've ever bought a loot crate, you know what to expect. Personally, I'm chasing Funkos. I love having them in my office and a few around my house. Like Loot Crate, you have to get the right box at the right time to really feel like your investment in decoration or memorabilia was worth it. Otherwise, it's cannon fodder for a garage sale.

I've bought three of these Bounty Boxes. The first was the Jabba Skiff box. I was a little disappointed. Who wants a Klaatu funko - literally reselling for 99 cents plus shipping on Ebay? The Lando Skiff Guard is cool I guess, but not something I would buy. Luckily, I got some shot glasses to drown my sorrows. $24 for the two funkos, $6 for the shot glasses, really not a bad deal if you squint your eyes and like the funkos.

I meant to cancel my subscription but wound up getting the Dagobah box by mistake. Luckily, it has a pretty cool movie moment where Luke is looking at his own head in the cave. YES! This is what i wanted. $30 for a movie moment is what you would pay in retail. To get a keychain and a miniature Yoda bobble, gravy.

I bought my third box after it had been released for $39.99. I really wanted the "Boba's Bounty" movie moment. I think this may be my strategy moving forward. Pay $10 more and only get the boxes that I want. $40 is a steep price for a funko, but i think it could increase in value and even if it doesn't, it looks awesome and I have a few people ask where I got it, so bonus points.

Fast and (so far) yummy. I just got my first shipment of the Original box and I'm so thrilled I couldn't wait until I'd tried all of them to write a review. I've been in a tea rut for a while, since the two loose leaf shops in my area both closed down within a year of each other and I was excited to try new things.

First, they shipped the October box in plenty of time for me to get it at the beginning of the month and since I just subscribed, that seems like a pretty good response time. The October box consists of four offerings and so far I have only gotten to try one of them, but I'm in love already and I'm super-excited about the other three. I brew my own kombucha at home so I fully intend to use the Fujian Black they sent for that purpose (although I will try it hot, as normal before I do, but plain unflavored black tea isn't generally my favorite, so most likely this will be used for my brew). The one I have drank at the time of writing this review is the Simao Spring tips and I like it a lot more than I expected to. The bag describes it as having "notes of sweet potato, caramel, nuts, fruits and spices" and that is not a bad description for this tea at all. I'm a huge fan of "Goguma" (sweet potato) lattes and this remind me a lot of those, especially when mixed with a bit of heavy cream. The third bag is Kathmandu Cosmos, which is described as being a chai blend. I'm addicted to chai so I can't wait to try this one. Last is a the Pacific Peppermint, described as an herbal tea. It will be nice to have some peppermint around again, especially with the weather starting to cool down.

I love the speed these came in and the amount I got for the price. I tend to be a bit picky when it comes to tea and I've paid more money for less product and sometimes gotten less enjoyment from some of those past buys. According to the literature in the packaging Tea Runners will be coming soon to Amazon Prime, so I'm hoping that means if there is a sample I like, I'll be able to order it in larger amounts at some point in the future.

I'll update this review if anything particularly funky happens with my test sips of the other three teas but if I haven't updated in a few days, assume the best. It's early, but so far I highly recommend this subscription.

Iron Man 2. Way to go guys. Of all the movies out there you went with that. I guess I should be greatful it wasn’t Iron Man 3 but still. review_text:
Box contains toxic products! Please be careful!. I have been a subscriber for a while and have generally enjoyed their products. However, after spraying the attached dental spray in my dogs’ mouths, I noticed the ingredient Xylitol. This artificial sweetener is HIGHLY toxic in dogs. When speaking with someone at Box Dog she informed me that there is recent research which suggests trace amounts of xylitol are not dangerous. This study does not appear to take into consideration diet or medical conditions (like unregulated diabetes, which would exacerbate the affects potentially making even trace amounts poisonous) and appears to be fairly new (only a few years old). I am disappointed that the company chooses to incorporate controversial ingredients without any sort of disclaimer. The risk they take endangering animals and not educating their owners is mind blowing. Even if one dog in 2500 dies it’s too many (she mentioned over 2000 dogs have used this without any reported issues). I’m not interested in subscription boxes so I can experiment with new studies in reducing plaque on their teeth. No part of that is worth the chance of the potential long term damage trace amounts do to the animals. My vet has advised 48 hour monitoring to ensure my dogs are not at risk. I have unsubscribed from this service and hope that they rethink the moral obligations the company has as a trusted provider of pet products. There are plenty of dental sprays with no xylitol. If they are cost prohibitive, please don’t cut corners to create diversity in your boxes. I would rather have another bag of safe treats with no medical benefits than be tricked into feeding my dogs something potentially harmful and understudied in this context. If you choose to include this product moving forward, PLEASE PLEASE include some sort of card that alerts owners to the presence and controversy and directs them to the study via a QR code or something. I will be spending the next 2 days in the emergency vet for something that is probably no big deal, but because this isn’t a widely accepted study or a “fact” known throughout the medical community, this companies disregard for transparency will cost me almost $2,000.

EDIT: my dogs survived, as expected, and never showed any signs of any kind of issues. My vet has advised to throw this product away or put it in a box “until more research is done and published”.
product_name: BoxDog - Monthly Dog Subscription Box with 100% Handmade Trea...

Very good, might try the same company for different subscription. ***UPDATE: I have to dispute some of the reviews here about cost per ounce. The pricing here is fair for the quality you are getting. A 30-second Google search can confirm this. As an example, I love silver needle white tea and this runs around $6/oz whether I buy from a high-end tea subscription or a specialty bulk shop.

I've tried a few different tea subscriptions and this one was very good. I decided to splurge on the Pure Tea collection for a little more money since I had a gift card, and do a three month trial. The teas are, as advertised, excellent quality, and despite what other reviewers have said, I think you get a pretty generous portion in the samples. I don't know if these people are making pitchers of iced tea or what, but I'm able to get 5+ cups from each sample, and there are four samples in the shipment. I've tried other services that send you a tiny packet, enough for 2-3 cups max, with 6 samples in the box. I guess it depends what you prefer.

I'm a cook...and this is still worth it. Can you find your own recipes for free on the internet? Yes. Can you go to Walmart and get your own utensils for cheap? Yes. Raddishkids changed how my 11-year-old daughter taught herself to cook. She wanted recipes she could understand HERSELF. She wanted to be able to cook an entire meal without me hovering around her, telling her what to do, and explaining the recipes she found online. The recipes are clearly explained, colorful, easy, and they TASTE GOOD. We have just completed a year's subscription and signed up for another year. She has become confident in her cooking ability.

You are not paying $24 for a spatula. At first we thought some things had been left out of the package as we only saw one skein of yarn and found no pattern in the bag. We were wrong, but I’ll get to that part.

I sent Jenna a message providing my personal email address (spelled out with spaces) letting her know the issue and told her I’d be happy to send her a photo of what was sent so she could see what was missing if she wanted to email me there. This started a very interesting and fun (I thought so anyway lol) game of message tag where we both attempted to figure out how to fool the algorithm because Amazon removed the address from four different messages between us. I’m glad she has a sense of humor because my last one was a little ridiculous. 😂

Turns out it was a case of user error and the package had everything promised. The smaller skein was inside of the larger skein for a pretty presentation and the pattern was online...oops! 🙄

The fact Jenna was so willing to spend hours to do all of this messaging and then not tell me I should maybe try reading thoroughly before all of that just shows how awesome she is and how much she wants to ensure her customers are satisfied. The colors are beautiful and my mom is looking forward to using her yarn hooks and making something with it. If you are considering this subscription for yourself or someone else, you won’t find a better person or product.

Thank you so much Jenna!

Great activities!. These are great activities to do WITH your child. Yes, with your child. Chances are, unless they are at the older end of this age range they won't be able to do it independently (but really, what science experiments and lessons that teach can a 5 or 6 year old do independently???). You will have to help your child put together the seal in the first box (I haven't gotten the other boxes yet, so not sure on how independent those are) but once put together my daughter loved playing with it and we talked about what was happening and what potential and kinetic energy are. We played the game together and the game board has a nice envelope on the back to store the pieces - teach your child how to gently put them away and take them out and it will last awhile.

Don't purchase this if you are looking for something that your child will do independently. This is not what this was made to do. This subscription box was made to help you teach your child different science facts and to do science activities together which it does great at. The books and activities are well laid out and easy to follow along. My daughter loved reading the book (I upgraded to the deluxe version) which was very well made and should last awhile.

This gets 4 stars simply because of the quality of the materials. They are well printed and on good quality paper, but they are made of paper and cardstock and won't last long. But then again, I won't have to find a place to store them forever!

review_text:
mostly seems like a way for Amazon to clear out inventory. If you are a new collector, you are better off digging for used and other deals. If you don't know a lot of classic, then this may be a way to gain some exposure but the value is not very good as many items are cheaper by a couple dollars if purchased direct from amazon.

For those with medium to large collections already you will probably return 80-90% of what they send you. I have only kept 2 or 3 of the 10 or so they have sent and had ~250 records. Returns roughly were based on 1/3 not being something I wanted, 1/3 being something I already had, 1/3 being overpriced.

Will probably cancel in another month or two but was holding out for Amazon to make some improvements based on previous comments. Primarily, they need to have set date each month to review what they are going to send and have a deadline to skip. Currently it is random and you have to login to amazon and view orders and there is ~24 hours or so that you may be able to catch it and skip. Way too random. Seems strategic of amazon to ship things banking on people not returning them if they have in hand. This seems shady and ultimately is some plan for Amazon to clear out inventory that isn't selling.

Another change Amazon still hasn't added despite suggestions, is a swap option. If each month there was an opportunity to swap for a few other choices, maybe I wouldn't be sending so many back. This could possibly still help them clear out inventory as greater chance of something I could actually want.

Given the value is poor many months, it is hard to recommend this for any collector. If you are disciplined about returns and have a convenient way to return amazon orders, then you have nothing to loose and maybe the continued loss in shipping expenses will motivate Amazon to implement changes. Maybe not as Amazon could just pass along the increased cost to consumers and continue poor ethics in how they handle employees.

Best thing you can do is buy from local small record stores. To my ears, these classics sound better on original pressings so buy used if you can. Some remasters from the original tapes are great, but the technology of the time was optimized for the vinyl format and sound the bands wanted. Clean copies of used records can be found for better prices than many of these Amazon record of the month classics.

review_text: Still Hoping..... Just to establish my bona fides, I have been to Japan multiple times over the years for periods of up to 4-6 weeks. So I know my Japanese snacks. I purchased a 3-Bokksu subscription as a surprise gift for my family to cheer us up during Covid quarantine. First box--the classic--was fantastic. Excellent array, interesting snacks, things you would not find at a Japanese market in the U.S. 100% recommend, thoroughly enjoyed. The second box....Well, it was sakura (cherry blossom) themed for spring. Which is completely appropriate and understandable. The thing is, cherry and plum blossom snacks are just not that tasty, especially to an American palate. Mayn things tasted kind of like cough syrup, very chemical. Others tasted less like sour ume (plum) and more like shiso leaf (not a fan). Rather than eyeing that extra piece left over after we'd divided up a snack in that box we all "graciously" urged the others in the family to take it, no, really, please. So I would give box #1 5 stars and box #2 3 stars...at best. Also, there were several items in the sakura box that I'm pretty sure I could've gotten for under $5 at my local Japanese market in the U.S. So....I guess will see how box #3 is. I hope for the best.  i can't say, though, that  I regret my purchase so far--everyone has enjoyed the anticipation of getting the snacks, opening them, going through the ritual of trying them even if they weren't that great--but I really hope the next box meets the quality of the first one!

review_text:
Super fun way to learn to code!. My kids have worked a bit with Hour of Code through their school and liked it, so when I came across Bitsbox, I thought it would be a great way to continue to develop their interest in coding. When I showed them the Bitsbox website and asked if they were interested, my 12yo was sort of "meh" about it but my 8yo was really excited. When the first box arrived, the 8yo built her first app "Doggleheads" where you can make a dog's head bobble back and forth on its body like a bobblehead. When the 12yo saw it, he immediately wanted to try it too. They spent the next two hours coding and giggling over the set of apps included with the first box. When they were done with their creations, we were able to scan the QR code on the screen to send the apps to friends and family.

The first box included a getting started guide, a guide for parents, a bunch of full-color cards with apps the kids can code, and an "Apper Keeper" binder where you can keep the app cards. All you have to do is go to the website included, type in a 4-digit code for the app you want to build, and then follow the step-by-step instructions for coding the app. I think the part I love the most is that it's super simple to figure out, but with a basic foundation kids can really go nuts and customize the apps to the limit of their own creativity. My 8yo was happy mixing and matching different dog heads and bodies while my 12yo figured out how to make the dogs run around the screen, sing Christmas songs, and even explode when they ran into each other (these were not part of the instructions!) My 8yo was slower with coding because you have to type in each command and she's not as confident using a keyboard. This is different from Hour of Code which mostly uses visual blocks of code that kids move around rather than type in. But my 12yo was very quick and liked the speed and freedom of typing in whatever commands he wanted. For both of them, having the program indicate where they made an error was really helpful, and this helped show them the importance of precision with code where even a missing comma can make the entire program not work.

Compared to the $400+ local in-person coding classes I was also considering, the monthly subscription cost of Bitsbox is a great deal and the kids really didn't need any help figuring things out on their own. The only downside was they ran out of new apps to code in the first few days so are anxiously waiting for the next month's box. We would completely recommend trying it out!
product_name: Bitsbox - Coding Subscription Box for Kids Ages 6-12

review_text:
Not fun, and not buying another. OK I've beaten several escape rooms but the riddles here ruin the whole thing. Referring to "Escape from Howling Hotel." There's a difference between making a mental muscle riddle and just showing off as a know-it-all, and this game fails that hands down. Out of the 6 major riddles, 4 were completely unsolvable without looking in the cheat book. Each one required some "ah ha" moment to deduce what the hell the riddle author was thinking, and if that moment just, like, doesn't arrive...then you're stuck in a infuriating dead end.
The first riddle all by itself is convoluted enough to make you want to quit the game before you even begin. You'd think the game would ease you in gently, giving you a softball to get settled in and feel the rush of early success...but oh hell no. Contrary to more compassionate view, the game throws a three part monster riddle at you. Except it never tells you its in three parts. Except each part relies on a singular inspiration of "ah ha" that just may not ever arrive. "Inspiration" and "deduction" are NOT the same thing. Anyone can deduce, where you just grind muscle and put in the time an eventually you'll get it. Those are fun. But "inspiration" is pure pass or fail. Either you have a Eureka moment, THREE TIMES, or the game crashes and burns on the very first level.
The other riddles were just as bad.
One in particular, mentioned by other reviewers (deservedly so, as its preposterous), concerns a grandfather clock, and deducing that the author has some obscure and arcane "pseudonym" for grandfather clocks, a "pseudonym" which he never bothered to tell the rest of us. A "pseudonym" that I immediately googled to see what the flip the author was referring to...finding nothing. Its nonsense, the author made it up completely and just hoped real hard the players could read his mind.
FOUR riddles were like that. FOUR riddles were completely unsolvable and unplayable unless you read the authors mind. Each one requiring outrageous leaps of mental illogic to get anywhere.
The last puzzle of the game is also wrong. You have to arrange guests at a dinner table to certain restrictions, except the solution I came up was more accurate than what was in the clue manual.
I've had it. To scour over a riddle, to watch the clock tick by as you're getting nowhere and have to take the mental compromise of reading the cheat book....it just isnt fun. I've seen it done better. I had little to no fun playing Howling Hotel and fully recommend everyone else stay far away as well.
Never buying from them again.
product_name: Crated with Love

review_text:
Won't get you started.... First, what you see in the provided "example kits" picture is unfortunately all you will get. What you won't see is just how small those skeins of yarn are: Both easily fit in the palm of my hand at the same time. If you read the kit FAQ, it will say you need additional things to complete the entire project. When you get the kit, it will not iterate what those things are, so you have to keep referencing this listing to know. Also, all of those items will cost you more individually than what you got scammed into paying for two small skeins. You'll spend another $30-$50 to get the items listed. You can literally buy multiple pounds of yarn for the price of a single month of this subscription.

None of the squares in the blanket pattern contain anything special or unique, so there are a number of free tutorials (both video and blog-style) that can teach you the same techniques and more. This also means that if you are advanced or want to learn more/get ahead, you're stuck waiting for the next month as there is no enrichment provided or go out on your own anyway.

I totally understand it takes quite a bit of time to produce the videos, money to house them, etc. if you want to run your own system, but there just isn't enough value for $30/month/person.. maybe $10-15/month would be more reasonable with an option to do a minimum 3-month subscription to get all the items you need to actually get started.

review_text:
Packaging can definitely be improved. Here's what I like: The price and ease of purchase that comes with a subscription. I can have succulents that I can use as gifts for clients or friends and it's a nominal cost.

Here's what I don't like: I don't know if it's the packaging or the way the plants are positioned in the boxes or what - but so far I received 2 BADLY broken plants. In each shipment there is at least a little bit of leave dropping or breakage.

These photos are of 2 separate deliveries. I watched the "bring my plant back to life" video on the site and from there it is all about patience. The leaves will start to grow roots, and then you can replant them. For the bunny ear cactus (in the box), only one of the broken leaves grew roots and the plant itself seems OK. With this latest shipment and the broken Mexican Snowball, if those leaves root successfully I could have like 8 plants. That said, I think wrapping the whole planter and around the plant itself will do more to protect during shipping than just the little bit of wrap around the stem.

Because I like container gardening, I don't mind doing the repotting and waiting it out to see if the broken leaves grow - I also turn it into a lesson with my kids. However, I am paying for 2 plants to arrive by mail monthly, so the 3-stars is because I've received 4 shipments and 2 BADLY broken plants.
product_name: Succulent Studios Subscription Box

review_text:
Hidden fees, pay to read one sentence, not solve a murder. As I understood from the site, the box's purpose was to solve a mystery. Instead, we found the murder weapon in <5 minutes in one piece of evidence (coroners report with the attached items at the scene). That's not hunting a killer, that's reading a sentence. So we submit the murder weapon in <5 minutes (we're not geniuses, btw so it would take anyone <5 minutes) and we're right. So we get an email to order the next box to pay another $30 to guess the motive (which we also figured out in this box, so why would we pay $30 next month)?!?

We solved the entire mystery from the box but now we need to pay another fee for the next box to take a guess at motive, killer, etc. Why include 9 pieces of evidence when you only need one to solve each episode?

I would not have purchased this subscription had I understood it would be 4+ boxes or >$120 to solve a mystery. I would have gladly paid more up front to solve the entire mystery and not spread out over 4 boxes. Instead, I feel misled by the description and brand.

If you're okay with paying >$100 to hunt a killer, not $30, this might be for you. For me, it's a waste of money and dishonest brand.

review_text:
i see a lot of potential for this club, if QUALITY and VALUE is sustained. I liked the value and quality of the first item I received with this club: I got The Clash London Calling 2xLP, the 2015 European pressing. Good value because the item usually costs about $32, but I was only charged $24.99 through this Club. Good quality because I checked the online reviews for this pressing at Discogs and elsewhere, and it seems to be widely praised.

My expectation - not a "hope," this is what I *expect* - is that this $24.99 a month program will consistently offer LP selections that normally cost $30 or more at Amazon or elsewhere. I will be disappointed and feel taken advantage of, if I am ever charged $24.99 for an item that I could purchase independently for $25 or less at Amazon or elsewhere.

Also, I was disappointed when I received this LP because the packaging was insufficient to prevent a serious corner crunch (see photo). This is the first LP I've received from Amazon that uses the "Lil Packaging" brand of vinyl mailer. Usually in my experience, Amazon has been using a brand-less option, with "wings" inside the interior of the packaging, that have done a consistently excellent job of holding the LP securely, and there are exterior "flaps" that help cushion against corner impacts. I have already sent feedback to Lil Packaging directly to encourage them to improve the design of their vinyl mailers.

I hope that the Lil Packaging brand is not going to be used with Club shipments in the future, as receiving damaged LPs every month will not be worth $24.99, regardless of how easy it is to return them.

review_text:
Love coffee? Tour the world of coffee from your kitchen. I received a monthly subscription to Driftaway Coffee and it’s a perfect gift for a coffee lover like me, who wants delicious coffee and the chance to educate my palate while exploring coffees from around the world. Driftaway provides the monthly coffee samplers, virtual tastings led by an expert (Brewer’s Cup Champion, no less!), detailed information about each coffee and the growers/collectives, and an opportunity to provide feedback to Driftaway so they can tailor future explorer boxes to your tastes. They also provide guides and information online to help you make a great cup with any coffee maker, while growing your knowledge.

All that and everything in the kit is sustainably sourced, from the compostable packages to the fair pricing and support of the farmers. As an independent, self-funded business they are walking the talk in their relationships with the farmers, their staff, and their clear commitment to give their customers a world-class, globetrotter’s experience of great coffee every month.
If you love coffee, Driftaway is absolutely the best way to learn at your own pace, month by month, while sipping some really exceptional coffee. I can’t wait for next month’s installment!

review_text: This is the gift to give YOURSELF!. I originally signed up for TheraBox as a once-a-month gift to myself after seeing the great reviews online.  I have kept it because it was so much more than what I expected!  Outside of the subscription box gifts that I expect and appreciate as part of a subscription plan, it has truly been a blessing to me and my mental health.  It allows me to build myself emotionally and mentally in a private way that is respectful of my faith without being faith-based.  I have been so encouraged by the care in the positive notes and activities and have seen a jump in my mental care and emotional growth.  This is the beauty of what this box was curated for.  I receive fun gifts to try and use monthly -and since I know another box is coming in thirty days I push myself to spend time using the products and take care of myself more often and better, inside and out.  There are a variety of products each time and I have found high-quality items mixed in with simple products -which is great because it meets my needs on a variety of levels.  This is the only box I have recommended to others and would do so again.  I justify the monthly cost because, well...it's cheaper than therapy but it meets my needs at that level.  This is not a box of "stuff".  This is mindfully put together to give back to other organizations (many of the products sent are from environmentally or socially conscience companies), to encourage the receiver to grow mentally/emotionally and to pamper the recipient.  The products are on-time and so far always packed well so nothing is broken.  Every time I read the pamphlet inside which explains the theme and products, but especially for a note from the  TheraBox Team which always begins with "Hello! Beautiful Soul" -just makes me smile.  Thank you to TheraBox for the love and care in your box!

Crap. Utter and complete crap.. EDIT: I took the 16 records I received from these goof-balls to my local used record store. Imagine yourself at a flea market. But not the nice kind with hippies, organic farmers and local artisans. I'm talking about the ones with meth addicts looking for arbitrage opportunities and purveyors of stolen goods. Now imagine you happen upon a stand selling used records. But not just any records... these are like from your Aunt Tonya's basement. You know, K-tel, K-mart clearance, really crappy Columbia House releases that Aunt Tonya got in 1973 because she was too lazy to send back her card and decline the monthly selection. review_text: All good things must come to an end. I've been receiving the Allure Beauty Box for months and I've loved it.  Yes, I've gotten more mascaras than I really need, but my general takeaway was really positive month to month.  I've received products that I didn't know I needed in my life, and a few months ago I loved the month where they did all different sheet masks.  I was super looking forward to every month and even when the boxes weren't spot on, I felt like I was getting my $15 worth.  However, starting at the new year they've began shipping the subscriptions in these "makeup pouches".  First of all, both months the pouches have arrived broken.  That's not even a big deal because I have enough makeup pouches as it is.  My bigger issue is that this is such an obvious attempt at masking the fact that they're decreasing the value of each month's products under the guise of a free makeup pouch.  In these two months I've thought the products have been redundant (a vitamin C serum both months) and each product (on average) is about half the size of what I was receiving before.  I was disappointed after receiving January's box and thought maybe my observations were a one-off, but given the fact I was a hardcore fan of my allure subscription I decided to give February's box a second chance and was disappointed again.

Good products, but unreliable shipping and almost non-existent customer service from Allure. I received the February box as my first shipment and while I like the products, I have had a huge problem with shipping and customer service.

This was irritating, but I know mistakes happen so I contacted Allure to receive a replacement.

Turns out, the replacement took nearly two weeks to arrive and when it did, the bag was ripped to the point of being unusable (very poor quality) and I was missing one of the items. I have since contacted Allure again and am hoping they will send me the item I am missing, but I'm doubtful at this point.

The proof is in the Grandkids. Can I add a couple more stars to my rating...5 just doesn't seem like enuf

I told them to have patience while we watched the video for the first lesson. We watched the first lesson together; although my granddaughter had already grabbed her chromebook from school and was through the first 3 lessons, successfully, before we finished the video. My grandson was so eager to get started that he could not sit still in his chair.

Additionally, after returning home the following morning from a sleepover; the first thing out of their mouths were; 'where is bitsbox?' My granddaughter is doing a 'row a day'; there are four stored programs in each row...so within 24 hours she had already created 8 programs...and they all worked. My grandson had a few challenges with wanting to experiment more than simply just typing in the provided code...but will a little help from Grampa he was back on the road to successful programming.
The first set of lessons is teaching them scripting syntax by rote...thru examples...but they are encouraged to experiment...to try to break it if you will...the mark of ALL good programmers...grin...these are two skills set needed for any programmer...the other is understanding logic and then in turn how to apply logic to programming...I imagine this will be discovered as they move thru the lessons...
FANTASTIC Program by Bitsbox...the grandkids were creating and destroying apps; literally within minutes... no wonder they were so eager to work with it.

Maybe the funko magic is fading. Had a subscription prior to Amazon taking over the shipping. Wife got me a new subscription for Christmas and I was pretty excited to see what would show up.

First off I assumed that Amazon would speed up the shipping, but that's not the case as the box still takes about a week to show up, and when it does its a box inside of a box, inside of another box. Pretty excessive if you ask me.

The actual contents this month were underwhelming, maybe funko is running out of ideas. A Jabbas skiff could pack a bit more luster given the iconic scene from Jedi, but instead I got a "mystery" mini that was obviously gonna be Jabba based on the theme and packaging. toothpick holders, aka shot glasses,and a Boba Fett luggage tag which goes great with my Death Star tag from a few months back. I'll hold out hope for the February box, but if the boxes remain underwhelming I'll likely cancel and go back to grabbing random pops as add on items to orders.

One person gives a question from the card, and the second person must come up for 4 question before the timer runs out. We got bored and stopped after a few minutes. Instead of a treat is came with the smallest fondue set I have ever seen. It might hold maybe four tablespoons. I am unsure if the candle that came with it would of warmed anything. So I did not try it. It also came with a tea size candle, you know the ones you can get for 50 cents.

Not for us. I was very excited when I ordered this subscription for my 10-year-old son who loves all things STEM. What a disappointment when our first shipment arrived. The product, a "Mechanics: Levers, Linkages & Structures" building set is accompanied by a VERY DENSE booklet explaining basics machines. At the very end of this book are a few building activities for basic structures. My problems with this are:
1) I don't know about most 10-yr-olds, but mine certainly doesn't want to sit down and read a textbook on levers. He just wants to build and play.
2) The suggested structures are the end of the book are a bit boring -- a seesaw, wheelbarrow, scale, parking gate, etc.
3) The book even includes a quiz -- if this doesn't scare kids off I don't know what will.
4) The pieces are really hard to put together.

After working together for about 10 minutes to build the seesaw, my son complained that his hands hurt, ran off and started doing something more interesting.

I'd save your money and choose STEM toys on your own that are sure to appeal to your particular child's likes and dislikes.

Unrealized Potential. The entire concept is definitely a great idea, and my son is well aware each month he's going to get a new STEM toy. Just seeing his excitement around what's coming for him is enough to keep the subscription going for now. At this age, we just want to make sure he's developing a love for STEM.

As a former science teacher, the quality of the actual toys/sets/kits selected could be so much better. The very first one was fantastic - it had three small "science fair" like experiments we did together in our kitchen, and each one had a sticker-like badge to give him upon completion. We were all excited about building a sense of cumulative growth by putting his badge stickers in his journal each month to see how many cool things we'd do. But alas, that great setup was only with the first manufacturer, and since then it has been a mix of items from many different manufacturers. Some are amazing, like a coding mouse + maze game. Others are pretty disappointing, like a big experiment kit that required buying additional supplies for every experiment. I'm hoping the quality of the monthly STEM Club goods increases soon. I'm not sure how long my son's (or my) excitement will last.

Fantastic experiments and learning. I subscribed to this recently, and want to share my experience. I have 10yo old son. I got the first box with two experiments - foam eruption and snake. And this is really exciting! From my son's perspective, it's fun to conduct these experiments like a real chemist: mix powders, pour chemicals into flask, shake, set on fire. And the result is amazing: this funny reactions last for some time to really enjoy them.

I enjoyed detailed description of how the reactions work, ion/cation, formulas that I mostly forgot since school. I tried to explain some of this to my son: I'm happy that he now knows how water breaks molecules into ions. But most of these will be interesting for high school kids.

Description doesn't say it, but I liked that every experiment has enough chemicals to run it at least twice(!). More, I'm surprised that all chemicals are safe and can be found at home: soap, citric acid, baking soda, food colorant and etc. I wish the box to have matches in it, but I guess some regulations ban it.

review_text:
Easy discounts. Service has potential. No risk with free returns for records you don't want.. So far, I've been in this for two months. First month was The Clash - London Calling. Second month was a Frank Zappa in New York live album. Not really a Zappa fan, so choose to cancel the order before it was shipped. It seems that each record can still be different month to month, as I saw The Clash and Pink Floyd for someone's July/Aug. Others got CCR instead of Zappa. Some people are getting duplicates, which really shouldn't be an issue and is on Amazon to make sure a month isn't wasted on a duplicate/rejected album.

I think to keep costs down, having a choice might not be an option. But I feel with a free return/cancel there's no real problem, outside of not getting a record, but at least you haven't paid for nothing. You have to be quick to cancel before an order is shipped, having the Amazon app helps out to get notifications when it is added to your orders to review prior to shipping and cancel. But even if I missed a cancel, I could just return the unopened record. Just requires a trip to the local Amazon approve shipping location, which takes some time out of my day.

Ideally, it would be nice to have a choice between 2-3 albums and/or having replacement for prior month ROTM. It would be nice to substitute a current month with a prior month's ROTM if you do not like it at a bare minimum. It would be nice to have genres of music to pick from at a later point to help with less choice rejections. There would be nice selections that can do 80's/90's as well.

Deceptive Billing, Lackluster Products. I originally signed up for this subscription for a promotion they were offering and to check out what types of items they ship out

I placed my original order on January 3rd, 2020 for $38.75 and got it today. I have to say that for the almost $40 I paid, I got maybe less than half that in value of what was inside.

But that's not the only thing I got today. I also received the surprise of ANOTHER $40 charge on my card. Mind you, this is less than two weeks after my first "monthly" payment.

When contacting them about it it turns out that if you order on the 3rd, you also get billed on the 15th for a box (full to the brim of what I'm sure are the finest products China has to offer) that you won't receive for another month.

This information is provided exactly nowhere when signing up, and instead must be found in their FAQs section of their website. While perusing their FAQs selection, also be sure to read the part where they DO NOT offer refunds, explicitly stating that this is because they CAN NOT guarantee your satisfaction

All in all, you're probably better off wearing a blindfold and grabbing $40 in random accessories off the shelves of your local sporting goods store. Not only will you get more bang for your buck, but you'll also have better customer service and return options.

Great replacement to my old Marvel Teeblox subscription - for the most part. ** Edited ** - I need to add that the December short has been a disappointment since its a Christmas theme and it hasnt arrived and as of Dec 24, hasnt even shipped. Its estimated arrival date is now Jan 4th - so why bother sending a Christmas Themed shirt in January?? Its a bummer that the December delivery has been handled so poorly - no reason it could be shipped before Christmas in an attempt to have it for Christmas.

I used to love my Marvel TeeBlox subscription until they decided to drop the Marvel subscription for a bunch of lame generic shirts. I tried Lootcrates Marvel box and even the tee box subscription - Loot crate was okay 2 years ago, but they changed and seem to send lower quality items and the shirt designs are boring, and one shipment was the same shirt from a few months earlier in a different color - So I have been hoping to find a new tee subscription for Marvel gear - and I finally did.

I stumbled on this one while looking around Amazons monthly subscription services on tee-shirts and toys. Decided, Why not try this one for a few months - This is my third month and all three shirts have been great quality with equally as great designs. I like that they use any Holidays in the month to theme the shirt that is sent - The Halloween shirt was my first one and it was a great design. It wasn't Halloween themed directly, but since it had the Green Goblin as the villain it had pumpkins in the design. November was just X-Men, but a good design and great color shirt - December is Christmas themed with Deadpool (and a funny shirt overall).

Could you get a shirt you dont like? Sure - Its a blind box subscription and it will happen. I dont think this should upset anyone, you should know this when you sign up for a mystery type of service. If you dont like one of the shirts, you can always send it back - You cant do that will Lootcrate or other monthly mystery boxes.

In the end, its a great service to receive a monthly "mystery present" - but at least you know it will be a quality shirt and theres a good chance it will have a great design based on Marvel.

review_text:
Don't waste your time or your money. I was gifted a six month subscription and was beyond excited for it. Having previously read reviews about how frustrating it was to have to wait for the next box; I waited until I had the full set before sitting down to "play" with a friend. To say I was disappointed would be an understatement.

The items sent in each box were generally a handful of printouts and a sprinkling of plastic garbage from a bulk retailer. The story often felt forced to bend around and include whatever random favor they threw in the box that month.

The clues in some instances required huge bodies of knowledge the average person doesn't have, or giant leaps to reach the expected conclusion.

Some examples:

1. A 1.5 inch piece of plastic thread taped to the back of an astronomy themed postcard. Apparently I was too know the postcard depicted Orpheus in constellation and the plastic tubing was also to indicate a link to Orpheus and his musical talents. What was the significance of Orpheus? Simply to let you know to continue looking forward. Irrelevant to the game's overall solution.

2. a postcard showing the name of a city. This was included to confirm the writer's previous claims of being from that city. How that confirms anything is beyond me.

3. A printout of some email correspondence between two people. This was too prompt you to email one of the parties yourself so that you could receive an automated response with more information. Because when I play a game that advertises "everything you need to solve the case is in the box" I automatically think about how I'm going to have to email fictional characters as part of the game play.

While playing it also became clear that things were missing. Some boxes lacked all the items they were supposed to come with. I ended up finding that out when I was finally able to locate lists of what each box should contain online. review_text:
We Love It. We really enjoy this company and their products. First, if you aren't familar, the idea is each season is 6 "episodes", and you get one episode per month. The premise is that a small town investigator doesn't have the resources to solve a murder, and they are enlisting your help (you being a more seasoned investigator). If you actually order through the Hunt a Killer website, you can expedite your boxes if you want to go through them faster. The Hunt a Killer website also has other seasons, entire box sets, and shorter non-subscription premiums of all kinds if you prefer harder mysteries, or science fiction, or paranormal, or family-friendly, etc. Many of the episodes have a goal of eliminating a suspect or two, but you shouldn't stop just at that. The people who finish each episode in 20 minutes must not be reading everything and finding all the clues. You should take notes and make timelines, as you will fill in time gaps and catch characters in lies or misinformation later as more evidence comes in with interviews and phone records, etc. You are piecing together a crime story with many characters, events, timelines, and items. The "small town investigator" sends you bagged evidence, interviews, autopsy reports, drug test results, maps, newspaper clippings, crime scene pictures, etc each month as they find them. There are website links to follow with surveillance footage, or recorded audio, or social media postings from the suspects, or high school discipline records. There are clues hidden in everything they send. There are ciphers to figure out. The attention to detail is unbelievable. Additionally, I can't relate to the people who said their customer service was bad. I emailed their website and had a response in a day. I posted a question in their Facebook group and was answered by one of their reps in less than one hour. Overall, it usually takes the two of us 90 minutes per episode (or box). I think $30 is reasonable for 90 minutes of entertainment for two people. We would spend that much or more if we went out somewhere for our entertainment instead. We recently bought The Woods box set of 5 episodes for $140 and the first box took us almost 3 hours! There were so many layers to it. It was so fun though because it was just like being in a horror movie (it was a paranormal story about witches summoning spirits). Overall, you get out of it what you put into it. If you are one dimensional and don't piece all aspects of the story together and only focus on eliminating one suspect, then you're not going to like it and you will sell the whole experience short. If you like challenging yourself and looking at all the angles, details, and storylines, you will love it too.

If you are considering it, I would recommend joining their official Facebook group. The reps will answer any questions and you can see how other people like it.
product_name: Hunt A Killer

review_text:
RaddishKids has impacted my kids culinary skills!. We have received the RaddishKid box for six months now. While it does not include ingredients, I find the boxes we've received valuable. My daughters have prepared recipes they would not have created otherwise.

My teenage daughters will have a plethora of recipes to take into adulthood with them.

I find the boxes simpler to use than searching online or cookbooks. In the past, I have bought cookbooks for my daughters, and they did not prepare nearly as many recipes from them as they have from the boxes we've received. I believe it's because the recipes are selected and tasteful. Yes, the boxes are more expensive than a recipe book, but an unused book isn't helping us reach our cooking goals. Plus, most recipe books for kids we've purchased seem to use prepared ingredients versus cooking from scratch.

As far as the apron, you will receive it if you order a 6 or 12 month paid in full subscription from their site directly. The month to month box does not include the apron. We didn't need the apron so it's not a big deal. They do sell them separately on their site though.

We usually receive our box mid-month from Amazon. This works well for us because the recipes can be created at anytime.

If you're looking to get your kids in the kitchen without hassle, consider RaddishKids. It's a simple way for them to gain autonomy in the kitchen and learn some new recipes. They may also find their favorite meal in a box. My daughter cooks one of the recipes at least twice a month because she likes it so much!

review_text: I feel bad leaving a bad review, I like Funko, but I’m disappointed... It didn’t meet my expectations.  The Deadpool box was my first one, and I canceled my subscription the day I received my box.  The Funko vinyl was good, but the rest of the items really felt like they were an afterthought.  I did put the luggage tag on my bag, and it stayed on during my last trip, but it’s doesn’t feel all that secure or well made.  The small window area for my information isn’t very large and didn’t line up with the insert for my info.  The keychain was alright I guess, but again if feels flimsy and not well made.  The metal screw drilled into the top to hold the keychain on has split the plastic apart and it’s loose.  I’d be afraid to actually use it as anything other than a decoration.  Maybe it’ll become a Xmas tree ornament.  Last, and least, was the plastic school bus taco holder... I can’t imagine anyone actually using that for its implied purpose.  It’s not really washable without ruining the stickers.  Even used as a phone holder as some people recommended doesn't really make it a worthwhile item.  If this box had included a decent T-Shirt, or if at least one of the other items felt thoughtful and well made, I’d have been much happier.  The whole box didn’t exactly feel like a real value.  I feel bad leaving a poor review because I do like the Funko company, but I’m still disappointed, whether rightfully so or not.

Young Entry Level Music Enthusiast will Love this. Veteran Music Lovers Can pass on this one.. Before I get into my review, here is what I have received so Far:

The Clash - London Calling
The Rolling Stones - Exile on Main Street
Diana Ross & The Supremes - Number Ones
Chronicle: The 20 Greatest Creedence Clearwater Rival Hits
Pink Floyd - Dark Side of The Month
The Who - Quadrophenia
Pink Floyd - The Wall (2016 Remaster)

First, the albums are without question great selections. For anyone just getting into vinyl, you’ll dig the selection. These albums are a great starter set.

However, variety of artists/bands and also omitting “greatest hits albums” would make this better. Veterans of vinyl or audiophiles can pass on this. I’ve gotten two Pink Floyd Albums so far. I’m not knocking Pink Floyd, absolute legends, but could we have picked just one album from them?

I haven’t received John Lennon, Aretha Franklin, David Bowie or Led Zeppelin yet. If you all provide feedback maybe this could be a 5/5 subscription. It just squeaks to an an average rating for me.

review_text:
I'm a newbie to vinyl collecting so this "club" seemed like a good fit. Joined in late November and got a record added to my cart a few days later, but it won't arrive until the very end of January. So a two month wait for The Who Sell Out...
In reading the other reviews it seems like not everyone gets the same record each month. Sounds like some people received The Who Sell Out a month or two before I joined.
So jury is still out... for a newbie with a starter collection like me this club could end up being good even if I get things people got months ago.
In doing more research after the fact it seems like this Amazon subscription (so far) is more basic than other monthly clubs. Nothing exclusive or special. The lack of transparency in selections (past, present, future) is odd and again makes me think we all don't get the same record each month.
The biggest concern for me is the other reviews saying that the monthly selection can at times be bought (on Amazon!) for less than the subscription price. If true that's pretty darn lame. Yes, there are remedies (like skipping that month's subscription and buying record for the lower price) but to have to jump through those extra hoops to get the best price on their own website just speaks to the level of effort getting put in on their side.
So again... jury is still out, but not off to a great start.
